Inf.description: Positive infinity; -Inf is negative infinity. n gives an n-by-n result; (m, n) or [m n] gives m-by-n; more sizes such as (m, n, p) give an N-D array. Example: 1/0 gives Inf.

MException.description: Creates an error value with identifier, formatted message and an empty stack field, ready to pass to throw. In mylab it is a plain struct, not an object.

NaN.description: Not-a-Number, the result of undefined operations such as 0/0. n gives an n-by-n result; (m, n) or [m n] gives m-by-n; more sizes such as (m, n, p) give an N-D array. NaN is unequal to everything, itself included; test for it with isnan.

abs.description: Absolute value of each element; for complex x, the magnitude. Example: abs(3 - 4i) is 5.

usage: A = accumarray(subs, vals, sz, fun, fillval)
accumarray.description: Groups the values vals by the subscripts in subs and combines each group. Each row of subs is one subscript (a column of indices for a vector result, two columns for a matrix, or a cell of index vectors). sz fixes the output size ([] lets the largest subscript decide). fun is called with each group's values as a column and must return a scalar (default: sum); if it returns a cell such as @(x) {x}, the result is a cell array. Positions that receive no values hold fillval (default 0, or [] for cells). Example: accumarray([1; 2; 1], [10; 20; 30], [], @max) is [30; 20].

acos.description: Inverse cosine in radians. Inputs outside [-1, 1] give complex results.

acosh.description: Inverse hyperbolic cosine. Inputs below 1 give complex results.

addpath.description: Adds folders to the front of the search path used to find .m files. A single argument may list several folders separated by the system path separator. Flags such as '-end' are ignored, so folders are always added at the front.

addvars.description: Appends variables (columns) to the right of a table.

airy.description: Airy functions: k = 0 gives Ai (default), 1 its derivative, 2 Bi, 3 the derivative of Bi. The third argument 1 returns the exponentially scaled version.

all.description: True if every element is nonzero, tested down columns for a matrix, along dim, or over 'all' elements. all([]) is true.

and.description: Same as A & B (element-wise logical AND).

angle.description: Phase angle of each complex element in radians, between -pi and pi.

annotation.description: Draws a shape on the figure (not tied to axes) in normalized figure units from 0 to 1. x = [x1 x2] and y = [y1 y2] give the start and end points; pos = [left bottom width height].

anova1.description: One-way analysis of variance: tests whether several groups share the same mean. Groups are the columns of y, or are given by labels in group (numbers, a char matrix or a cell array). tbl is the ANOVA table as a cell array; stats holds the group names, sizes and means. No figure is shown.

any.description: True if at least one element is nonzero, tested down columns for a matrix (a row of results), along dim, or over 'all' elements. any([]) is false.

area.description: Plots the curve y and shades the region between it and zero. Only a single vector is supported. Returns a graphics handle when an output is requested (see get and set).

array2table.description: Turns each column of the matrix A into a table variable.

arrayfun.description: Calls f on each element of one or more same-size arrays, the way cellfun does for cells. Elements of a struct array are passed as 1-by-1 structs and elements of a cell array as 1-by-1 cells. Example: arrayfun(@(k) k^2, 1:3) is [1 4 9].

asin.description: Inverse sine in radians. Inputs outside [-1, 1] give complex results.

asinh.description: Inverse hyperbolic sine of each element.

assert.description: Throws an error if cond is false (or not all true). The default message is 'Assertion failed.'; a custom message and identifier follow the same rules as error.

atan.description: Inverse tangent in radians, between -pi/2 and pi/2. See atan2 for the full circle.

atan2.description: Four-quadrant angle in radians, between -pi and pi, of the point (x, y). Note that y comes first. Inputs expand against each other. Example: atan2(1, -1) is 3*pi/4.

atan2d.description: Four-quadrant inverse tangent like atan2, but the result is in degrees.

atanh.description: Inverse hyperbolic tangent. Inputs outside (-1, 1) give complex or infinite results.

autumn.description: n-by-3 colormap from red through orange to yellow.

usage: axis([xmin xmax ymin ymax zmin zmax])
axis.description: Sets axis limits or appearance. An Inf or -Inf limit keeps that end automatic, e.g. axis([0 Inf 0 Inf]). 'equal' makes units the same length on both axes, 'image' does that and fits the data tightly, 'square' makes the plot box square, 'tight' fits the limits to the data, 'off' hides the axes, 'auto' restores automatic limits, 'normal' also undoes 'equal' and 'square', 'ij' puts the y origin at the top and 'xy' back at the bottom. With an output and no input, returns the current limits.

bar.description: Vertical bar chart of y, at positions x or 1..n. A matrix y draws groups of bars, one group per row and one colour per column, or stacks them with 'stacked'. width is the fraction of the space each group fills (default 0.8). Options: FaceColor, EdgeColor, LineWidth, FaceAlpha, DisplayName. b is a Bar handle (a row array of them for a matrix y).

barh.description: Horizontal bar chart; takes the same inputs and options as bar.

beep.description: Accepted for compatibility; makes no sound.

besseli.description: Modified Bessel function of the first kind I_nu(z); 1 returns the exponentially scaled form.

besselj.description: Bessel function of the first kind J_nu(z), element by element. The third argument 1 returns the exponentially scaled version. Results may be complex for negative z.

besselk.description: Modified Bessel function of the second kind K_nu(z); 1 returns the exponentially scaled form.

bessely.description: Bessel function of the second kind Y_nu(z). Negative z gives complex results; 1 scales.

beta.description: Beta function, gamma(a).*gamma(b)./gamma(a+b), element by element.

betacdf.description: Beta distribution cumulative probability. Add 'upper' as the last argument to get the upper tail 1 - P.

betainc.description: Regularized incomplete beta function for x in [0, 1], lower tail by default or upper tail with 'upper'.

betapdf.description: Beta distribution density on [0, 1] with shape parameters a and b.

bin2dec.description: Value of a binary digit string; spaces are ignored. Example: bin2dec('101') is 5.

binocdf.description: Binomial probability of at most x successes in n trials. Add 'upper' as the last argument to get the upper tail 1 - P.

binopdf.description: Binomial probability of exactly x successes in n trials with success probability p. Example: binopdf(1, 2, 0.5) is 0.5.

binornd.description: Binomial random counts for n trials with probability p.

bitand.description: Bitwise AND of non-negative integer values; the result is double.

bitcmp.description: Bitwise complement of non-negative integers within the width of the integer class (8, 16, 32 or 64 bits).

bitget.description: Value (0 or 1) of bit number bit (1 = least significant) of each non-negative integer in a. Example: bitget(6, 1:3) is [0 1 1].

bitor.description: Bitwise OR of non-negative integer values; the result is double.

bitset.description: Sets bit number bit of a to 1 (or to value, 0 or 1). Example: bitset(8, 1) is 9.

bitshift.description: Shifts the bits of integer values left by n places (right when n is negative). n must be a scalar. Example: bitshift(1, 3) is 8.

bitxor.description: Bitwise exclusive OR of non-negative integer values; the result is double.

blackman.description: Blackman window of length n as a column vector.

bone.description: n-by-3 greyscale colormap with a slight blue tint.

bounds.description: Smallest and largest elements of x in one call, ignoring NaN. mylab always looks at all elements; a dimension argument is not supported.

box.description: Shows or hides the top and right edges of the current axes' frame; box alone toggles. The axes property Box does the same.

bsxfun.description: Expands singleton dimensions of A and B so their sizes match, then calls the binary function f once with the expanded arrays. Plain operators already expand like this, e.g. A - mean(A).

butter.description: Butterworth filter design (maximally flat IIR filter) of order n. Wn is the cutoff as a fraction of the Nyquist frequency (between 0 and 1); a two-element Wn designs a band-pass filter. ftype is 'low', 'high', 'bandpass' or 'stop'. 's' designs an analog filter with Wn in rad/s. Example: [b, a] = butter(4, 0.2) is a 4th-order low-pass filter for use with filter.

cart2pol.description: Converts Cartesian coordinates to polar (or cylindrical): theta is the angle in radians and rho the distance from the origin. A single matrix with 2 or 3 columns may be given and, with one output, a matrix of the same layout is returned.

cart2sph.description: Converts Cartesian coordinates to spherical: azimuth in the x-y plane, elevation from that plane (both in radians) and radius.

cast.description: Converts x to the named class: 'double', 'single', 'logical' or an integer class.

cat.description: Joins arrays along dimension dim: 1 stacks them vertically, 2 side by side, 3 stacks them as pages of an N-D array, and so on. Sizes must agree in every other dimension.

cd.description: Changes the current working folder (a leading ~ means your home folder). With no input, prints or returns the current folder.

ceil.description: Rounds each element up, toward +Inf. Example: ceil(2.1) is 3.

cell.description: Cell array whose cells all hold the empty matrix []. cell(n) is n-by-n.

cell2mat.description: Concatenates the contents of a cell array into one array, joining each row of cells side by side and then stacking the rows. The pieces must fit together. Example: cell2mat({1 2; 3 4}) is [1 2; 3 4].

cell2struct.description: Builds a scalar struct whose fields, named by a cell array (or a single name), take their values from the cells of C in order. A dimension argument and struct-array results are not supported.

cell2table.description: Makes a table with one variable per column of the cell array C. Columns holding only numeric scalars become numeric variables; others stay cell columns.

celldisp.description: Prints the contents of every cell, labelled like C{1} or C{2,3}, descending into nested cell arrays. name replaces the label 'C'.

cellfun.description: Calls f on the contents of each cell (on matching cells of several same-size inputs). By default every call must return a scalar and the results form an array the size of C; with 'UniformOutput' false they are collected in a cell array. f may be a handle or a function name; the names 'isempty', 'length', 'numel', 'isreal', 'islogical' and 'ndims' are handled directly. An error handler h is called with an error struct and the inputs. Example: cellfun(@numel, {'ab', 'c'}) is [2 1].

cellstr.description: Converts text to a cell array of char vectors: each row of a char matrix becomes one cell (trailing blanks removed), giving a column; a string array gives a cell array of the same size (<missing> becomes ''); a cell array is returned as is.

char.description: Makes a char array. Numbers are taken as character codes. A cell array, a string array or several text inputs become rows of a char matrix, padded with spaces to equal length. Example: char(72, 105) is a two-row char array; char([72 105]) is 'Hi'.

cheby1.description: Chebyshev Type I filter design: order n, Rp decibels of ripple allowed in the passband, and a sharper roll-off than Butterworth. Wn and ftype work as in butter.

chi2cdf.description: Chi-square cumulative probability with nu degrees of freedom. Add 'upper' as the last argument to get the upper tail 1 - P.

chi2pdf.description: Chi-square density with nu degrees of freedom.

usage: y = chirp(t, f0, t1, f1, method)
y = chirp(t, f0, t1, f1, method, phi)
chirp.description: Swept-frequency cosine whose frequency moves from f0 at time 0 to f1 at time t1 (defaults 0, 1 and 100 Hz). method is 'linear' (default), 'quadratic' or 'logarithmic'; phi is the initial phase in degrees.

chol.description: Cholesky factor of a symmetric positive definite matrix: upper triangular R with R'*R = A, or lower triangular L with L*L' = A. If A is not positive definite it is an error, unless p is requested: then p is nonzero and R is empty (mylab does not return a partial factor).

circshift.description: Shifts elements circularly by k places, wrapping the ones that fall off the end back to the start. Without dim the shift follows the first dimension whose size is not 1; a two-element shift moves rows and columns. Example: circshift([1 2 3], 1) is [3 1 2].

cla.description: Removes everything drawn in the current axes, keeping the figure and any other axes.

class.description: Name of the type of x as a char vector, for example 'double', 'char', 'logical', 'int8', 'cell', 'struct', 'string' or 'function_handle'. Objects report their class name, such as 'table', 'containers.Map' or the name of a classdef class.

clc.description: Clears the command window when the host program supports it; otherwise does nothing.

clear.description: Removes variables from the current workspace: all of them, the named ones, or those matching a wildcard pattern. 'clear all' also clears globals and closes figures; 'clear global' removes global variables. 'clear functions' is accepted and does nothing.

clearvars.description: Removes variables from the current workspace: all of them, the named ones, or those matching a wildcard pattern. 'clear all' also clears globals and closes figures; 'clear global' removes global variables. 'clear functions' is accepted and does nothing.

clf.description: Clears everything from the current figure, or from figure handle f.

clock.description: Current local date and time as [year month day hour minute seconds].

close.description: Closes the current figure, figure number n, figure handle(s) f, the figure with the given Name, or every figure.

colon.description: Function form of the a:b and a:step:b range operators. Returns a row vector, empty when the range runs the wrong way or the step is 0.

colorbar.description: Adds a colour scale beside the current axes for the most recent image, surface or contour plot (or for the colormap alone). location is 'eastoutside' (default), 'westoutside', 'northoutside' or 'southoutside'. c is a ColorBar handle: c.Label.String sets its label, and Limits, Ticks, TickLabels and FontSize can be read and set. colorbar off removes it.

colormap.description: Sets the colour map of the current figure, recolouring its images and surfaces and those drawn later. name is a colormap name such as 'parula' (the default, drawn with matplotlib's viridis), 'jet', 'hot', 'gray' or any matplotlib colormap; map is an m-by-3 matrix of RGB values in [0, 1], e.g. jet(16). target may be an axes or figure handle. With an output, returns the current map as a matrix (256 rows for named maps).

complex.description: Builds a complex array a + b*i. With one input the imaginary part is zero but the result is still stored as complex, so isreal reports false.

compose.description: Formats data into text with sprintf-style conversions, giving one piece of text per row rather than one long result. With a single array, each row is fed to the format, using as many columns per piece as the format has conversions; with several arrays, matching elements are formatted together. Returns a cell array of char vectors, or a string array when fmt is a string. Example: compose('%d-%d', [1 2; 3 4]) is {'1-2'; '3-4'}.

computer.description: Name of the platform as reported by Python, e.g. 'linux', 'darwin' or 'win32'. These codes differ from the architecture strings other implementations use.

cond.description: 2-norm condition number, the ratio of the largest to smallest singular value. Large values mean that solving with A loses accuracy. Other norms are not supported.

conj.description: Complex conjugate of each element: the sign of the imaginary part is flipped.

containers.Map.description: Creates a map from keys (char vectors or numbers) to values. Read and write entries with m(key) and m(key) = value; use keys(m), values(m), isKey(m, k), remove(m, k) and m.Count. A map is a handle: copying the variable shares the same map.

contains.description: True if s contains pattern anywhere. pattern may be a cell or string array, meaning any of them. s may be a cell or string array, giving a logical array.

contour.description: Draws contour lines (lines of equal height) of Z, optionally over the grid X, Y, with n levels or at the given level values (also 'LevelList'). 'ShowText', 'on' labels the lines; 'LineColor' and 'LineWidth' style them. Replaces the current axes unless hold is on. Returns a graphics handle when an output is requested (see get and set).

contourf.description: Like contour, but fills the regions between the contour lines with colour.

conv.description: Convolution of two vectors, which is also polynomial multiplication. shape is 'full' (default, length numel(u)+numel(v)-1), 'same' (central part the size of u) or 'valid'. The result is a column if u is a column. Example: conv([1 1], [1 -1]) is [1 0 -1].

conv2.description: Two-dimensional convolution. shape 'full' (default) returns the whole result, 'same' the central part with the size of A, and 'valid' only the part computed without zero padding. With two vectors u and v, A is convolved with column u and then with row v.

cool.description: n-by-3 colormap from cyan to magenta.

copper.description: n-by-3 colormap from black to a light copper colour.

corr.description: Linear (Pearson, default) or rank (Spearman) correlation between the columns of X, or between each column of X and each column of Y. Kendall's tau is not supported.

corrcoef.description: Pearson correlation coefficients between the columns of X (or between x and y), with ones on the diagonal. P holds p-values for testing zero correlation. Name-value options are ignored.

cos.description: Cosine of each element, with x in radians.

cosd.description: Cosine of angles given in degrees. Odd multiples of 90 give exactly 0.

count.description: Number of non-overlapping occurrences of pattern (or of any pattern in a list) in s. A cell array of text gives an array of counts. Example: count('banana', 'an') is 2.

cov.description: Covariance. For a vector, the variance; for a matrix whose columns are variables, the covariance matrix; for two vectors, their 2-by-2 covariance matrix. w = 1 normalizes by N instead of N-1. 'omitrows' drops rows containing NaN.

cputime.description: Processor time used by mylab so far, in seconds. Differences between two calls time code.

cross.description: Cross product of two 3-element vectors, shaped like a. Matrix inputs are not supported. Example: cross([1 0 0], [0 1 0]) is [0 0 1].

csvread.description: Reads a comma-separated numeric file; empty fields become 0. r and c are zero-based row and column offsets of the first value to read.

csvwrite.description: Writes a numeric matrix as comma-separated values with five significant digits; r and c shift the data down and right, padding with zeros.

ctranspose.description: Same as A' : swaps rows and columns and conjugates complex values.

cummax.description: Running maximum along the first dimension whose size is not 1, or along dim. Example: cummax([1 3 2 5]) is [1 3 3 5].

cummin.description: Running minimum along the first dimension whose size is not 1, or along dim.

cumprod.description: Running product along the first dimension whose size is not 1, or along dim.

cumsum.description: Running total along the first dimension whose size is not 1, or along dim. 'reverse' accumulates from the end. Integer inputs keep their class and saturate. NaN flags are accepted but have no effect. Example: cumsum([1 2 3]) is [1 3 6].

cumtrapz.description: Running trapezoid-rule integral, same size as y and starting at 0. Uses unit spacing or the points in x, along the first dimension whose size is not 1.

datestr.description: Formats a serial day number (now if omitted) as text like '05-Mar-2024 14:07:30' in local time. A format argument is not supported.

dbcont.description: At the K>> prompt: continue running until the next breakpoint.

dbdown.description: Not supported: the K>> prompt always works in the paused function's workspace.

dbquit.description: At the K>> prompt: stop the program.

dbstack.description: Shows the functions currently being run, innermost first, or returns them as a struct array.

dbstatus.description: Lists the breakpoints, or returns them as a struct array.

dbstep.description: At the K>> prompt: run the next line (stepping over calls), step into a function, or run until the current function returns.

dbstop.description: Sets a breakpoint: the program pauses with a K>> prompt when it reaches that line. Needs an interactive terminal. In the web app, use Step through instead.

dbup.description: Not supported: the K>> prompt always works in the paused function's workspace.

deal.description: Copies inputs to outputs: one input is copied to every output; otherwise there must be as many inputs as outputs and each goes to its own output.

deblank.description: Removes trailing whitespace and null characters only.

dec2bin.description: Binary representation of the non-negative integer d as a char vector, zero-padded to at least n digits. Only scalar input is supported. Example: dec2bin(5) is '101'.

dec2hex.description: Hexadecimal representation (upper-case digits) of the non-negative integer d, zero-padded to at least n digits. Only scalar input is supported. Example: dec2hex(255) is 'FF'.

decimate.description: Reduces the sample rate by the integer factor r after low-pass filtering: by default an 8th-order Chebyshev Type I filter applied forward and backward (zero phase), or a 30-tap FIR filter with 'fir'. n changes the filter order.

deconv.description: Polynomial division: b = conv(a, q) + r. r has the same length as b, padded with leading zeros.

deg2rad.description: Converts angles from degrees to radians (multiplies by pi/180).

delete.description: Deletes the named file(s), or, for a handle object, runs the class's delete method (if any) and marks the object invalid so later use raises an error. For graphics handles (from plot, figure, legend, ...) the object is removed from its plot; deleting a figure closes it.

det.description: Determinant of a square matrix. Example: det([1 2; 3 4]) is -2.

detrend.description: Removes the best-fit straight line (default), mean ('constant') or polynomial of degree n from a vector or from each column of a matrix. Breakpoints are not supported.

deval.description: Evaluates a solution structure from an ODE solver at the times t, using the solver's own continuous interpolant, so the values are as accurate as the solution itself. Each column of y is the state at one time; idx selects components and yp holds the derivatives. Times must lie within the solved interval.

diag.description: For a vector v, builds a square matrix with v on the k-th diagonal (k = 0 main, k > 0 above, k < 0 below). For a matrix A, extracts the k-th diagonal as a column vector. Example: diag([1 2]) is [1 0; 0 2].

diff.description: Differences between neighbouring elements, x(2)-x(1), x(3)-x(2), ..., along the first dimension whose size is not 1 unless dim is given. n repeats the operation n times, so the result is n elements shorter. Example: diff([1 4 9]) is [3 5].

dir.description: Lists a folder, the files matching a wildcard pattern such as '*.csv', or a single file. With an output, returns a column struct array with fields name, folder, date, bytes, isdir and datenum. A folder listing includes '.' and '..'.

disp.description: Print the value of x without showing a variable name. An empty char prints a blank line; other empty values print nothing. Example: disp('hello') prints hello.

display.description: Prints x the way an unterminated statement would, with an 'ans =' header.

dlmread.description: Reads a delimited numeric file; empty fields become 0. r and c are zero-based offsets.

dlmwrite.description: Writes a numeric matrix to a delimited text file (comma by default; '\t' or 'tab' for tabs). precision is a number of significant digits or a format such as '%.3f' (default five significant digits).

doc.description: Same as help: prints the help text in the command window (no browser is opened).

dot.description: Dot product. For two vectors with the same number of elements, sum(conj(a).*b); for matrices, the dot products of matching columns as a row vector. A dim argument is not supported.

double.description: Converts to double precision. Char input gives character codes; a string or string array is parsed as numbers element by element (NaN where the text is not a number or is <missing>). Cells and structs cannot be converted. Example: double('A') is 65; double("2.5") is 2.5.

drawnow.description: Updates figure windows so that pending drawing appears, e.g. inside an animation loop. shg and refresh do the same.

e.description: Euler's number 2.71828..., the base of the natural logarithm. Same as exp(1).

eig.description: Eigenvalues of a square matrix as a column vector, or eigenvector matrix V and diagonal eigenvalue matrix D with A*V = V*D. With B, solves the generalized problem A*V = B*V*D. Symmetric (Hermitian) input gets real eigenvalues in ascending order; for other matrices the order and eigenvector scaling may differ from other implementations.

ellipke.description: Complete elliptic integrals of the first (K) and second (E) kind for parameter m in [0, 1]. A tolerance argument is not supported.

endsWith.description: True if s ends with pattern (or any pattern in a cell array). Works element-wise on a cell array s.

envelope.description: Upper and lower envelopes of a signal from the magnitude of its analytic signal, centred on the mean. Only the 'analytic' method is supported; a window length argument is ignored.

eps.description: With no input, the gap between 1 and the next larger double, about 2.2204e-16. eps(x) gives that gap at the magnitude of each element of x. eps('single') gives the single-precision gap.

erase.description: Deletes every occurrence of pattern (or of each pattern in a list) from the text. s may be a char vector, a string, a string array or a cell array of text; string input gives string output. Example: erase('a-b-c', '-') is 'abc'.

erfc.description: Complementary error function, 1 - erf(x), accurate for large x.

erfcinv.description: Inverse complementary error function; defined for y in [0, 2].

erfinv.description: Inverse error function; defined for y in [-1, 1].

error.description: Throws an error that stops the program unless caught by try/catch. The message is formatted like sprintf when extra arguments or escapes are present. A first argument such as 'pkg:name' (with a colon and no spaces) followed by more text is taken as the identifier. A struct with message and identifier fields can be passed instead. error([]) does nothing.

errorbar.description: Plots y with vertical error bars, of half-length err or with separate lower and upper lengths neg and pos. Returns a graphics handle when an output is requested (see get and set).

etime.description: Seconds elapsed from date vector t0 to date vector t1 ([year month day hour minute seconds], as returned by clock).

eval.description: Runs text as code in the current workspace. If it fails and catchcode is given, that is run instead. With outputs, code must be a single expression whose values are returned. Building variable names with eval is error-prone; prefer arrays, cells or structs.

evalc.description: Runs text as code and returns everything it would have printed, as a char vector.

exist.description: Tells what a name refers to: 1 for a variable, 2 for a file or a function defined in a .m file or in the session, 5 for a built-in function, 7 for a folder, 0 if not found. kind ('var', 'file', 'dir' or 'builtin') limits the search.

exit.description: Ends the mylab session, optionally with a numeric exit status for the operating system.

exp.description: e raised to the power of each element. Example: exp(0) is 1.

expcdf.description: Exponential cumulative probability with mean mu (default 1). Add 'upper' as the last argument to get the upper tail 1 - P.

expint.description: Exponential integral E1(x), the integral of exp(-t)/t from x to Inf. Negative real x gives complex results.

expm.description: Matrix exponential of a square matrix (not the element-wise exp).

expm1.description: exp(x) - 1 computed accurately when x is tiny.

exportgraphics.description: Saves the figure containing obj (a figure or axes handle, e.g. gcf or gca) to an image file, with the format taken from the extension. The whole figure is saved, even for an axes. Other options are accepted and ignored.

exppdf.description: Exponential density with mean mu (default 1); note mu is the mean, not the rate.

exprnd.description: Exponential random numbers with mean mu.

extractAfter.description: Text after the first occurrence of pattern, or after character position pos. If the pattern does not occur the result is empty text. s may be a char vector, a string, a string array or a cell array of text; string input gives string output.

extractBefore.description: Text before the first occurrence of pattern, or before character position pos. If the pattern does not occur the result is empty text. s may be a char vector, a string, a string array or a cell array of text; string input gives string output.

extractBetween.description: Text between start and end markers (excluded unless 'Boundaries' is 'inclusive'), or between two character positions (both included). For a char vector every match is returned as a column cell array; for a cell array each element must contain exactly one match. Example: extractBetween('a[b]c[d]', '[', ']') is {'b'; 'd'}.

eye.description: Identity matrix: ones on the main diagonal, zeros elsewhere. A non-square size puts ones on the diagonal starting at the top-left. N-D sizes are not supported. Example: eye(2) is [1 0; 0 1].

factor.description: Row vector of the prime factors of the scalar n in ascending order, with repeats. Example: factor(12) is [2 2 3].

factorial.description: n! for each element of n, e.g. factorial(5) is 120. Returned as double.

false.description: Logical 0, or a logical array of zeros. n gives an n-by-n result; (m, n) or [m n] gives m-by-n; more sizes such as (m, n, p) give an N-D array.

fcdf.description: F distribution cumulative probability. Add 'upper' as the last argument to get the upper tail 1 - P.

fclose.description: Closes a file opened with fopen, or all of them. An unknown fid is an error.

feof.description: True if there is nothing more to read from the file.

feval.description: Calls the function f, given as a handle or a name, with the remaining arguments. Example: feval('max', [3 8 1]) is 8.

fft.description: Fast Fourier transform (discrete Fourier transform) along the first dimension whose size is not 1, or along dim; each column of a matrix is transformed. n zero-pads or truncates to n points. The result is always complex; abs(Y) is the amplitude spectrum. Example: fft([1 0 0 0]) is [1 1 1 1].

fft2.description: Two-dimensional fast Fourier transform of a matrix, optionally padded or cropped to m-by-n.

fftshift.description: Swaps the halves of a spectrum so the zero-frequency term sits in the middle, which suits plotting fft output against centred frequencies.

fgetl.description: Reads the next line from a file without its line ending. Returns -1 at end of file.

fgets.description: Reads the next line from a file, keeping its newline. Returns -1 at end of file.

fieldnames.description: Field names of a struct as a column cell array of char vectors, in creation order.

figure.description: Opens a new figure, or makes figure n (or figure handle f) current, creating it if needed. Later plots go to the current figure. f is a Figure handle with properties such as Number, Name, Color and Position, which may also be given as Name/Value options; other common window options (e.g. 'NumberTitle', 'Visible', 'Units') are accepted.

fileparts.description: Splits a file path into its folder, base name and extension (with the dot). Example: fileparts('a/b.txt') gives 'a', 'b' and '.txt'.

fileread.description: Entire contents of a text file (read as UTF-8) as one char vector.

fill.description: Draws a filled polygon with corners (x(k), y(k)); c is a colour name or RGB triplet, and matrix x, y draw one polygon per column. fill replaces the plot unless hold is on; patch always adds to the current axes. Options: FaceColor, EdgeColor, FaceAlpha, LineWidth, DisplayName. Returns a graphics handle when an output is requested (see get and set).

fillmissing.description: Replaces missing entries. Methods: 'constant' (the value v), 'previous', 'next', 'nearest' and, for numeric data, 'linear', 'spline', 'pchip' and 'makima'. Matrices are filled column by column (or along dim); tables variable by variable. Leading or trailing gaps are extrapolated by the interpolating methods unless 'EndValues' is 'none', 'nearest' or a constant. TF marks the entries that were filled. Example: fillmissing([1 NaN 3], 'linear') is [1 2 3].

filter.description: Applies the rational digital filter with numerator b and denominator a to the data x, along a row vector or down the columns of a matrix. Initial conditions are not supported. Example: filter(1, [1 -0.5], [1 1 1]) is [1 1.5 1.75].

filtfilt.description: Zero-phase digital filtering: runs the filter forward and then backward, so the output has no phase delay and the filter's effect is squared. Works along a row vector or down columns. The data must be longer than three times the filter order.

find.description: Linear indices of the nonzero elements of x, in column-major order. n limits the result to the first (or 'last') n hits. With two or three outputs, returns row and column subscripts and the values. The result is a row for row-vector input, otherwise a column. Example: find([0 5 0 7]) is [2 4].

findgroups.description: Numbers the groups formed by the unique values (or unique combinations of values) of the grouping vectors, in sorted order of those values. G gives the group number of each element (NaN when a value is missing); ID holds each group's value. Works for numeric, logical, cell arrays of text and string vectors, and for all variables of a table. Example: findgroups([5 3 5]) is [2 1 2].

findpeaks.description: Finds local maxima (peaks) of a vector: points higher than both neighbours, with a flat top reported at its first sample; the end points are never peaks. locs are indices, or positions from x (a scalar x is a sample rate). Options: MinPeakHeight, MinPeakProminence, MinPeakDistance, Threshold, SortStr ('ascend'/'descend') and NPeaks. Widths, prominences and plotting are not supported. Example: findpeaks([1 3 2 5 1]) is [3 5].

fix.description: Rounds each element toward zero, dropping the fractional part. Example: fix(-2.7) is -2.

flintmax.description: 2^53, the largest value up to which every integer is exactly representable as a double. A class argument is not supported.

flip.description: Reverses the order of elements along the first dimension whose size is not 1, or along dim. Example: flip([1 2 3]) is [3 2 1].

fliplr.description: Reverses the order of the columns (left-right mirror). Works on cell arrays too.

flipud.description: Reverses the order of the rows (up-down mirror). Works on cell arrays too.

floor.description: Rounds each element down, toward -Inf. Example: floor(-2.5) is -3.

fminbnd.description: Minimizes a function of one variable on the interval [a, b] (golden section search with parabolic steps). output holds iterations, funcCount, algorithm and message.

usage: x = fmincon(fun, x0, A, b, Aeq, beq, lb, ub)
x = fmincon(fun, x0, A, b, Aeq, beq, lb, ub, nonlcon)
fmincon.description: Constrained nonlinear optimization: minimizes fun(x) from the start x0 subject to linear constraints, bounds and nonlinear constraints, where nonlcon returns [c, ceq] with c <= 0 and ceq = 0 required. Uses sequential quadratic programming with numerical gradients and finds a local minimum. Only the MaxIterations (or MaxIter) option is read. exitflag is 1 on success, -2 if the result is infeasible.

fminsearch.description: Minimizes a function of several variables without derivatives (Nelder-Mead simplex), starting at x0. Options TolX, TolFun, MaxIter and MaxFunEvals are read. output holds iterations, funcCount, algorithm and message.

usage: [x, fval, exitflag, output, grad, hessian] = fminunc(...)
fminunc.description: Minimizes a smooth function of several variables without constraints (quasi-Newton BFGS). grad is the gradient and hessian an approximation of the Hessian at the solution.

fopen.description: Opens a text file and returns a file id (3 or higher) for fprintf, fgetl, fgets, feof and fclose, or -1 on failure with the reason in msg. permission is 'r' (default), 'w', 'a', 'r+', 'w+' or 'a+'; a 't' or 'b' suffix is accepted. Files are read and written as UTF-8 text.

format.description: Chooses how many digits numbers display with: long shows about 15 significant digits, short (the default) about 5. 'compact' and 'loose' are accepted but change nothing.

fpdf.description: F distribution density with nu1 and nu2 degrees of freedom.

fplot.description: Plots the function handle f over the interval [a b] (default [-5 5]) by sampling it at many points; f is called with a vector and, if that fails, one point at a time. With two handles draws the parametric curve (fx(t), fy(t)).

fprintf.description: Formats data like sprintf and writes it out. Without a file id, or with fid 1 or 2, the text goes to the command window; otherwise to a file opened with fopen. No newline is added automatically. The optional output is the number of bytes written.

freqz.description: Frequency response of a digital filter at n points (default 512) from 0 up to the Nyquist frequency ('whole' goes around the full circle). w is in radians per sample, or f in Hz when the sample rate fs is given. A vector of frequencies may be given instead of n. No plot is drawn; plot abs(h) yourself.

fscanf.description: Reads formatted data from the rest of an open file, like sscanf: conversions such as %d, %f, %g and %s are applied repeatedly. size may be n, Inf or [m n] (with n possibly Inf) and fills the result column by column.

fsolve.description: Solves the system of equations f(x) = 0, starting from x0. f returns a vector of residuals. Options are ignored.

full.description: Returns its input unchanged, since mylab has no separate sparse storage.

fullfile.description: Joins folder and file names with the operating system's separator. Example: fullfile('data', 'run1.csv') is 'data/run1.csv' on Linux.

func2str.description: Text form of a function handle: the function name, or the full expression starting with @ for an anonymous function.

fzero.description: Finds a zero of a function of one variable, starting from x0 (a sign change is searched for around it) or inside the interval [a b] whose ends have opposite signs. output holds iterations, funcCount, algorithm and message.

gamcdf.description: Gamma cumulative probability with shape a and scale b (default 1). Add 'upper' as the last argument to get the upper tail 1 - P.

gamma.description: Gamma function of each element; gamma(n) equals factorial(n-1) for positive integers.

gammainc.description: Regularized incomplete gamma function: the lower tail P(a, x) by default, or the upper tail 1 - P with 'upper'. Note that x comes first. a must be non-negative.

gammaln.description: Natural log of the gamma function, useful when gamma itself would overflow.

gampdf.description: Gamma density with shape a and scale b (default 1).

gca.description: Handle to the current axes, creating a figure and axes if needed. Its properties (XLim, YLim, Title, XLabel, FontSize, XScale, Box, XGrid, XTick, XTickLabel, ...) can be read and set with dot syntax or get/set, and most plotting functions accept it as their first input.

gcd.description: Greatest common divisor of corresponding integer elements of a and b.

gcf.description: Handle to the current figure, creating one if none exists. f.Number is its figure number; the handle works with get, set, saveas, print and close.

get.description: Reads a property of a graphics handle h (from gcf, gca, plot, title, ...). Property names ignore case. When h holds several handles (e.g. all lines returned by one plot call) the result is a cell array with one row per handle. get(h) returns a struct of the common properties. A figure number or 0 (the graphics root) also works as h. Dot syntax, e.g. h.LineWidth, reads the same properties.

getenv.description: Value of an operating-system environment variable, or '' if it is not set.

getfield.description: Value of the named field, the same as s.(name). Only a single field level is supported.

gradient.description: Numerical derivative: central differences in the interior and one-sided differences at the ends. Spacing may be a scalar step or a vector of coordinates. For a matrix, gx differentiates along each row (across columns) and gy along each column. Example: gradient([1 4 9 16]) is [3 4 6 7].

gray.description: n-by-3 colormap of greys from black to white (default 256 rows).

grid.description: Shows or hides grid lines on the current axes; grid alone toggles.

groot.description: Handle to the graphics root, the parent of all figures (the same as handle 0). Its properties include CurrentFigure and ScreenSize.

groupsummary.description: Summary statistics for each group of table rows. The result has one row per group with the grouping values, a GroupCount column and one column per method and data variable, named like mean_Height. Methods: 'mean', 'sum', 'min', 'max', 'median', 'mode', 'std', 'var', 'range', 'numel', 'nnz', 'nummissing', 'all', or a function handle; NaN values are left out of the statistics. datavars defaults to all other numeric variables.

hamming.description: Hamming window of length n as a column vector.

hann.description: Hann (raised-cosine) window of length n as a column vector; the end points are zero.

hanning.description: Hann window variant without the zero end points, as a column vector.

head.description: First k rows of a table or array (default 8).

height.description: Number of rows of a table (or of an array).

help.description: Shows the calling forms and a short description of a function. For functions and classdef classes in your own .m files it shows the comment block at the top of the file. With an output the text is returned instead of printed.

hex2dec.description: Value of a hexadecimal digit string. Example: hex2dec('ff') is 255.

hilb.description: n-by-n Hilbert matrix with entries 1/(i+j-1), a classic badly conditioned example.

hilbert.description: Analytic signal of real data: the real part is x and the imaginary part its Hilbert transform, so abs(z) is the instantaneous amplitude. Works along a row vector or down columns; any imaginary part of x is ignored.

hist.description: Older histogram function using equal-width bins (10 by default) or bins around the given centres. With outputs it returns the bin counts (and centres) without plotting; without outputs it draws the bars. Use histogram for a graphics handle.

histc.description: Counts values falling in each interval edges(k) <= x < edges(k+1); the last count is for values equal to the last edge. bin gives each value's interval (0 if outside). Older function; histcounts is usually more convenient.

histcounts.description: Counts how many values of x fall in each bin; every bin includes its left edge and the last bin also its right edge. Automatic bins use a round width (1, 2, 2.5 or 5 times a power of ten) based on the spread of the data, with edges on multiples of it; integer data over a small range gets unit-width bins centred on the integers. Normalization may be 'count', 'probability', 'pdf', 'cdf', 'countdensity' or 'cumcount'. bin gives the bin number of each element (0 when outside). Example: histcounts(1:5) is [1 1 1 1 1] with edges 0.5:1:5.5.

histogram.description: Plots a histogram of the finite values in x. Bins are chosen automatically (unit bins for small integer data) unless a bin count or edges are given, or the options NumBins, BinEdges, BinWidth, BinLimits or BinMethod ('integers'). Normalization may be 'count', 'probability', 'percentage', 'countdensity', 'pdf', 'cumcount' or 'cdf'. Style options: FaceColor, EdgeColor, FaceAlpha, LineWidth, DisplayName, Orientation. h is a Histogram handle: h.Values gives the bar heights, and changing h.NumBins, h.BinEdges, h.BinWidth or h.Normalization redraws the plot.

hold.description: With hold on (or hold all), new plots are added to the current axes instead of replacing them; hold off returns to replacing. hold alone toggles. An axes handle selects other axes. The axes property NextPlot ('add' or 'replace') shows the same state.

home.description: Clears the command window when the host program supports it; otherwise does nothing.

horzcat.description: Joins arrays side by side, the same as [A, B, ...]. They must have the same number of rows.

hot.description: n-by-3 colormap from black through red and yellow to white.

hsv.description: n-by-3 colormap cycling through the hues of the colour wheel.

hypot.description: sqrt(a.^2 + b.^2) element by element, computed without overflow for large values.

i.description: The imaginary unit, sqrt(-1). Can be overwritten by a variable named i; writing 1i is safer.

idivide.description: Integer division with a chosen rounding: 'fix' (toward zero, the default), 'floor', 'ceil' or 'round'. At least one input must be an integer type (two integer inputs must share a class) and the result has that class. Example: idivide(int32(7), int32(2)) is 3.

ifft.description: Inverse fast Fourier transform. The result is returned as real when its imaginary parts are negligible; 'symmetric' always returns the real part.

ifft2.description: Two-dimensional inverse FFT; real output when the imaginary parts are negligible or with 'symmetric'.

ifftshift.description: Undoes fftshift (they differ for odd lengths).

imag.description: Imaginary part of each element (0 for real input).

image.description: Shows the matrix C as an image, mapping its value range (or [cmin cmax]) onto the current colormap; row 1 is at the top. x and y give the centres of the first and last columns and rows. image and imshow behave the same way in mylab. Returns an Image handle (CData) on request.

imagesc.description: Shows the matrix C as an image, mapping its value range (or [cmin cmax]) onto the current colormap; row 1 is at the top. x and y give the centres of the first and last columns and rows. image and imshow behave the same way in mylab. Returns an Image handle (CData) on request.

import.description: Accepted for compatibility so that code importing packages still runs. mylab has no package namespaces, so the statement has no effect.

importdata.description: Loads numeric text data. Without header lines the result is a matrix. With header lines it is a structure with data (the matrix), textdata (the header text) and, when the last header line names the columns, colheaders. The delimiter and number of header lines are detected when not given. .mat files are loaded as with load.

imshow.description: Shows the matrix C as an image, mapping its value range (or [cmin cmax]) onto the current colormap; row 1 is at the top. x and y give the centres of the first and last columns and rows. image and imshow behave the same way in mylab. Returns an Image handle (CData) on request.

ind2sub.description: Converts linear indices into subscripts for an array of size sz. With fewer outputs than dimensions, the last output counts through the remaining dimensions. Example: [r, c] = ind2sub([3 4], 8) gives r = 2, c = 3.

inf.description: Positive infinity; -Inf is negative infinity. n gives an n-by-n result; (m, n) or [m n] gives m-by-n; more sizes such as (m, n, p) give an N-D array. Example: 1/0 gives Inf.

innerjoin.description: Combines rows of two tables that have equal key values (by default all variables with the same name). Every matching pair of rows gives one output row; the result is sorted by key. Non-key variables of the right table are appended; names used in both tables get _left and _right suffixes. 'LeftVariables' and 'RightVariables' choose the variables to keep.

input.description: Shows prompt and reads a line from the user. The reply is evaluated as an expression, so typing 2*3 gives 6; an empty reply gives []. With 's' the raw text is returned instead.

insertAfter.description: Inserts new after every occurrence of pattern, or after character position pos. s may be a char vector, a string, a string array or a cell array of text; string input gives string output.

insertBefore.description: Inserts new before every occurrence of pattern, or before character position pos. s may be a char vector, a string, a string array or a cell array of text; string input gives string output.

int16.description: Converts to the int16 integer class: values are rounded to the nearest integer (halves away from zero), clipped to the range -32768..32767, and NaN becomes 0. Example: int16(2.5) is 3.

int2str.description: Rounds x to integers and converts the result to text like num2str.

int32.description: Converts to the int32 integer class: values are rounded to the nearest integer (halves away from zero), clipped to the range -2147483648..2147483647, and NaN becomes 0. Example: int32(2.5) is 3.

int64.description: Converts to the int64 integer class: values are rounded to the nearest integer (halves away from zero), clipped to the range about -9.2e18..9.2e18, and NaN becomes 0. Example: int64(2.5) is 3.

int8.description: Converts to the int8 integer class: values are rounded to the nearest integer (halves away from zero), clipped to the range -128..127, and NaN becomes 0. Example: int8(2.5) is 3.

usage: q = integral(f, a, b, 'AbsTol', at, 'RelTol', rt)
integral.description: Numerical integral of f from a to b by adaptive quadrature; a and b may be Inf or -Inf. mylab calls f with one scalar at a time, so f need not be vectorized. Other options such as 'ArrayValued' or 'Waypoints' are not supported. Example: integral(@(x) x.^2, 0, 3) is 9.

usage: q = integral2(f, xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax)
integral2.description: Numerical double integral of f(x, y) over xmin <= x <= xmax and ymin <= y <= ymax. ymin and ymax may be numbers or functions of x. f is called with scalars. Options are not supported.

interp1.description: One-dimensional interpolation of the samples (x, y) at the points xq. Methods: 'linear' (default), 'nearest', 'previous', 'next', 'spline' (not-a-knot cubic spline), 'pchip' and 'cubic' (shape-preserving piecewise cubic) and 'makima' (modified Akima). Outside the range of x the result is NaN for the first four methods and extrapolated for the cubic ones, unless 'extrap' or a fill value is given. If y is a matrix, each column is interpolated. Example: interp1([1 2 3], [10 20 30], 2.5) is 25.

usage: Zq = interp2(X, Y, Z, Xq, Yq)
interp2.description: Interpolation on a 2-D grid. X and Y are grid vectors or meshgrid matrices (default 1:n and 1:m). A row vector Xq with a column vector Yq is expanded to a grid. Methods: 'linear' (default), 'nearest', 'cubic', 'spline' and 'makima'. Points outside the grid give NaN or extrapval. interp2(Z, k) refines the grid by halving the spacing k times (once if k is omitted).

interpft.description: Resamples periodic data to n points by zero-padding (or trimming) its Fourier transform.

intersect.description: Values found in both a and b, without repeats, sorted unless 'stable' is given; c = a(ia) = b(ib). The result is a row unless a is a column. Accepts cell arrays of text. The 'rows' option is ignored. Example: intersect([3 1 2], [2 3 4]) is [2 3].

usage: x = intlinprog(f, intcon, A, b, Aeq, beq, lb, ub)
intlinprog.description: Mixed-integer linear programming: like linprog, but the variables listed in intcon must take integer values. Pass [] for constraints that are not needed. Options are ignored.

intmax.description: Largest value an integer class can hold, returned in that class. Defaults to 'int32'. Example: intmax('uint8') is 255.

intmin.description: Smallest value an integer class can hold, returned in that class. Defaults to 'int32'. Example: intmin('int8') is -128.

inv.description: Inverse of a square matrix, so that A*Y is the identity. A warning is printed when A is singular or nearly so, and the result is then unreliable (possibly Inf). For solving A*x = b, A\b is faster and more accurate.

ipermute.description: Undoes permute: ipermute(permute(A, order), order) gives back A.

iqr.description: Interquartile range: the 75th minus the 25th percentile, a spread measure robust to outliers.

is_function_handle.description: True if x is a function handle such as @sin or @(t) t.^2.

isa.description: True if class(x) equals classname. Also accepts the group names 'numeric' (double, single or integer), 'float' (double or single) and 'integer' (any integer class). For objects of a classdef class it is also true for any superclass, e.g. isa(dog, 'Animal').

iscell.description: True if x is a cell array.

iscellstr.description: True if C is a cell array in which every cell holds a char vector (or empty char).

ischar.description: True if x is a char array, e.g. text in single quotes.

iscolumn.description: True if A has exactly one column (a 0-by-1 array counts).

isdeployed.description: Always false: mylab code never runs as a compiled standalone application.

isdiag.description: True if every entry of the numeric matrix A off the main diagonal is zero.

isdir.description: True if f names an existing folder.

isempty.description: True if A has no elements, i.e. at least one dimension is 0.

isequal.description: True if all inputs have the same size and contents. Numeric type is ignored, so isequal(1, int8(1)) is true. NaN is never equal to NaN; see isequaln.

isequaln.description: Like isequal, but NaN values in matching positions count as equal.

isfield.description: True if s is a struct with a field of that name; a cell array of names gives a logical array. Non-struct input gives false.

isfile.description: True if f names an existing file (not a folder).

isfinite.description: Logical array that is true where x is neither NaN nor infinite.

isfloat.description: True if x is a double or single array.

isfolder.description: True if f names an existing folder.

isgraphics.description: True for each element of h that is a valid (not deleted or closed) graphics handle, optionally of the given type such as 'line' or 'figure'. Figure numbers count as handles of open figures. ishandle and ishghandle are the same.

ishandle.description: Same as isgraphics: true for valid graphics handles.

ishermitian.description: True if the square matrix A equals its conjugate transpose A' ('skew': equals -A'). With tol, small differences relative to the size of A are allowed.

ishghandle.description: Same as isgraphics: true for valid graphics handles.

ishold.description: True if hold is on for the current axes.

isinf.description: Logical array that is true where x is Inf or -Inf.

isinteger.description: True if x has an integer class such as int8 or uint32. A double holding a whole number is not an integer type.

iskeyword.description: True if s is a reserved word of the language such as 'for' or 'end'. With no input, returns all keywords as a column cell array.

isletter.description: True for each alphabetic character in a char array; false for non-char input.

islogical.description: True if x is a logical (boolean) array.

ismatrix.description: True if A has exactly two dimensions (any size, including empty).

ismember.description: True where an element of a is found in s; loc gives the index of the first match in s (0 when absent). Works for numbers, text and cell arrays of text. With 'rows', each row of A is looked up among the rows of B and column vectors are returned. Example: ismember([1 2; 5 6], [5 6; 0 0], 'rows') is [false; true].

ismethod.description: True if obj has a public method called name.

ismissing.description: True where an element is missing: <missing> in a string array, NaN in a numeric array, or an empty char vector in a cell array. Returns a logical array the size of x.

isnan.description: Logical array that is true where x is NaN.

isnumeric.description: True for double, single and integer arrays (real or complex). False for logical, char, cell, struct and string values.

isobject.description: True if x is an object: a containers.Map, a table, or an instance of a classdef class.

isprime.description: Logical array that is true where x is a prime number.

isprop.description: True if obj has a public property called name.

isreal.description: False only when x is stored as a complex array; a complex array whose imaginary parts are all zero still counts as not real. True for non-numeric values.

isrow.description: True if A has exactly one row (a 1-by-0 array counts).

issorted.description: True if the elements (or rows, with 'rows') are already in order. Other modes: 'strictascend', 'strictdescend' and 'strictmonotonic'. Works on cell arrays of text too.

isspace.description: True for each whitespace character in a char array; false for non-char input.

issparse.description: Always false: mylab stores every matrix densely.

issquare.description: True if A has the same number of rows and columns.

isstring.description: True if x is a string scalar, e.g. text in double quotes.

isstrprop.description: Tests each character of s for a category: 'alpha', 'digit', 'alphanum', 'wspace', 'upper', 'lower', 'punct' or 'cntrl'.

isstruct.description: True if x is a struct or struct array.

issymmetric.description: True if the square matrix A equals its transpose ('skew': equals minus its transpose). With tol, small differences relative to the size of A are allowed.

istable.description: True if x is a table.

istext.description: True if x is either a char array or a string.

istril.description: True if every entry above the main diagonal of the numeric matrix A is zero.

istriu.description: True if every entry below the main diagonal of the numeric matrix A is zero.

isunix.description: True when running on a POSIX system (Linux or macOS).

isvalid.description: True for a handle object (classdef handle class, containers.Map, ...) that has not been deleted with delete(h). For graphics handles it is false once the object has been deleted or its figure closed; for an array of graphics handles it returns one value per handle.

isvarname.description: True if s is a valid variable name: a letter followed by letters, digits or underscores, at most 63 characters, and not a keyword.

isvector.description: True if A is 1-by-n or n-by-1 with at least one element.

j.description: The imaginary unit, sqrt(-1). Can be overwritten by a variable named i; writing 1i is safer.

jet.description: n-by-3 rainbow colormap (default 256 rows) from dark blue to dark red.

join.description: Text: joins the strings in C with a delimiter (default a space) along the last dimension, or along dim. Tables: adds to each row of Tleft the variables of the row of Tright with the same key values (by default the variables with the same name); every left row must match exactly one right row, and the left row order is kept.

kaiser.description: Kaiser window of length n as a column; larger beta (default 0.5) gives lower side lobes.

keyboard.description: Pauses the program at this point and opens the K>> debugger prompt, where you can inspect variables, step (n, s) or continue (c). Only works in an interactive terminal; elsewhere it does nothing.

kmeans.description: k-means clustering of the rows of X into k groups. idx gives each row's cluster number, C the cluster centres, sumd the within-cluster sums of distances and D the distance from every point to every centre. Options: 'Distance' ('sqeuclidean' default or 'cityblock'), 'Replicates' (keep the best of several runs), 'MaxIter' (default 100) and 'Start' ('plus' k-means++ default, 'sample', 'uniform' or a k-by-p matrix). Rows with NaN get idx NaN. Results are random; set rng for repeatable runs.

kron.description: Kronecker product: every element A(i,j) is replaced by the block A(i,j)*B.

kurtosis.description: Sample kurtosis, a measure of how heavy the tails are; a normal distribution gives 3 (this is not the excess kurtosis). flag 0 applies the bias correction. NaN values are ignored.

lastwarn.description: Text of the most recent warning, or an empty char if there was none.

lcm.description: Least common multiple of corresponding integer elements of a and b.

ldivide.description: Same as A .\ B, i.e. B ./ A.

legend.description: Adds a legend naming the plotted items in drawing order, or only the graphics handles h. Without labels it uses each item's DisplayName, or data1, data2, ... legend off removes it, legend boxoff/boxon hides or shows its frame. Options: Location (a compass name such as 'northeast', 'southwest', 'best', or an outside position like 'eastoutside'), Orientation ('horizontal'), NumColumns, FontSize, Box, TextColor, Title. l is a Legend handle (String, Location, Box, FontSize, ...). With yyaxis, items from both sides are listed.

length.description: Size of the longest dimension of A, or 0 if A is empty. Example: length(ones(3, 7)) is 7.

line.description: Draws a line in the current axes without clearing it, whatever the hold state. A matrix draws one line per column. Accepts the same Name/Value options as plot.

lines.description: n-by-3 matrix repeating the default line colour order (default 7 rows).

usage: x = linprog(f, A, b, Aeq, beq)
x = linprog(f, A, b, Aeq, beq, lb, ub)
linprog.description: Linear programming: minimizes f'*x subject to A*x <= b, Aeq*x = beq and lb <= x <= ub, using the HiGHS solver. Pass [] for constraints that are not needed. exitflag is 1 when solved, 0 at the iteration limit, -2 when infeasible and -3 when unbounded (then x is []). An options argument is ignored.

linsolve.description: Solves the linear system A*x = b, the same as A\b. An options struct is not supported.

linspace.description: Row vector of n points evenly spaced from a to b, both ends included. n defaults to 100. Example: linspace(0, 1, 5) is [0 0.25 0.5 0.75 1].

load.description: Reads variables from a .mat file into the workspace, or into the fields of S when an output is given. Numeric data is loaded as double. A .csv, .txt or .dat file is read as a numeric matrix and stored in a variable named after the file (or returned).

log.description: Natural logarithm of each element. log(0) is -Inf and negative inputs give complex results.

log10.description: Base-10 logarithm of each element; negative inputs give complex results.

log1p.description: log(1 + x) computed accurately when x is tiny. Inputs below -1 give NaN.

log2.description: Base-2 logarithm of each element; negative inputs give complex results. The two-output form [f, e] = log2(x) is not supported.

logical.description: Converts to logical: nonzero becomes true, zero becomes false. NaN input is an error.

loglog.description: Like plot, but with logarithmic x and y axes.

logm.description: Matrix logarithm, the inverse of expm. May be complex.

logspace.description: Row vector of n points spaced evenly on a log scale from 10^a to 10^b. n defaults to 50. Example: logspace(0, 2, 3) is [1 10 100].

lower.description: Converts text to lower case, character by character, so the length never changes. Works on char arrays, strings, string arrays and cells.

usage: x = lsqcurvefit(fun, x0, xdata, ydata, lb, ub)
lsqcurvefit.description: Nonlinear curve fitting by least squares: finds parameters x so that fun(x, xdata) matches ydata as closely as possible, starting from x0. Uses Levenberg-Marquardt, or a trust-region method when bounds are given. Options StepTolerance (TolX) and FunctionTolerance (TolFun) are read. Example: lsqcurvefit(@(p, t) p(1)*exp(p(2)*t), [1 -1], t, y).

usage: x = lsqnonlin(fun, x0, lb, ub, options)
lsqnonlin.description: Nonlinear least squares: minimizes the sum of squares of the residual vector returned by fun(x), starting from x0, optionally within bounds. Methods and options as in lsqcurvefit.

lsqnonneg.description: Non-negative least squares: minimizes norm(C*x - d) subject to x >= 0. resnorm is the squared residual norm.

lu.description: LU factorization with partial pivoting. With three outputs, P*A = L*U where L is unit lower triangular. With two outputs, L already includes the row permutation, so A = L*U.

mad.description: Mean absolute deviation from the mean (flag 0, default) or median absolute deviation from the median (flag 1). NaN values are ignored.

mag2db.description: Converts amplitude ratio to decibels: 20*log10(m). Negative values give NaN.

magic.description: n-by-n magic square: every row, column and both main diagonals add up to the same value, n*(n^2+1)/2. Each integer 1..n^2 appears once. magic(2) is returned as [4 3; 1 2] even though no true 2-by-2 magic square exists.

makima.description: Modified Akima piecewise cubic interpolation, which avoids most overshoot without flattening the curve as much as pchip. Returns values at xq or a piecewise polynomial.

mat2cell.description: Cuts a 2-D array into blocks and returns them in a cell array. r lists the block heights and c the block widths; they must add up to the size of A (c defaults to all columns). Example: mat2cell(magic(4), [2 2], [3 1]) gives a 2-by-2 cell.

mat2str.description: Text that recreates A when evaluated, such as '[1 2;3 4]'. Uses up to n significant digits (15 by default). Logical values print as true/false and char input is returned in quotes.

max.description: Largest element along the first dimension whose size is not 1 (or along dim, or over 'all'). idx gives the position of the first maximum. NaN values are skipped unless every value is NaN; complex values are compared by magnitude. max(A, B) takes the larger of A and B element by element. Example: [m, i] = max([3 9 2]) gives m = 9, i = 2.

maxk.description: The k largest elements along the first non-singleton dimension (or dim), largest first. NaN values come last. I gives their indices. Example: maxk([3 9 4 7], 2) is [9 7].

mean.description: Arithmetic average, along the first dimension whose size is not 1 unless dim or 'all' is given. 'omitnan' ignores NaN values. The result is double, also for integer input; mean([]) is NaN. Example: mean([1 2; 3 4]) is [2 3].

medfilt1.description: One-dimensional median filter of order n (default 3): each output is the median of a window around the sample, which removes spikes while keeping edges. padding is 'zeropad' (default) or 'truncate'; 'omitnan' ignores NaN.

median.description: Middle value after sorting (the average of the two middle values for an even count), along the first dimension whose size is not 1 unless dim or 'all' is given. Any NaN makes the result NaN unless 'omitnan' is given.

mesh.description: Draws a 3-D wireframe surface in the current axes, replacing it unless hold is on. meshc currently draws the same plot without contour lines. Returns a Surface handle on request.

meshc.description: Draws a 3-D wireframe surface in the current axes, replacing it unless hold is on. meshc currently draws the same plot without contour lines. Returns a Surface handle on request.

meshgrid.description: Builds grid coordinates from vectors: each row of X is a copy of x and each column of Y is a copy of y, so X and Y are numel(y)-by-numel(x). Handy for evaluating a function of two variables over a grid. With three vectors it builds 3-D grids.

methods.description: Lists the public methods of an object or class; with an output, returns them as a cell column.

min.description: Smallest element along the first dimension whose size is not 1 (or along dim, or over 'all'). idx gives the position of the first minimum. NaN values are skipped unless every value is NaN. min(A, B) takes the smaller of A and B element by element.

mink.description: The k smallest elements along the first non-singleton dimension (or dim), smallest first. NaN values come last. Example: mink([3 9 4 7], 2) is [3 4].

missing.description: A missing value. Here it is a string scalar holding <missing>; ismissing(m) is true.

mkdir.description: Creates a folder, including any missing parent folders. It is not an error if the folder already exists. The optional output is true.

mkpp.description: Builds a piecewise polynomial. Row k of coefs holds the coefficients of piece k (highest power first) in the local variable x - breaks(k); d is the number of components for a vector-valued polynomial. Example: ppval(mkpp([0 1 2], [1 0; -1 1]), 1.5) is 0.5.

mldivide.description: Same as A \ B, which solves A*X = B (least squares if A is not square).

mod.description: Remainder after division, defined as a - floor(a./b).*b, so a nonzero result has the sign of b. mod(a, 0) is a. Example: mod(-1, 3) is 2. See rem for the truncating version.

mode.description: Most frequent value, along the first dimension whose size is not 1 unless dim is given. Ties go to the smallest value and NaN is ignored. Only the first output is supported.

more.description: Accepted for compatibility; output is never paged, so it does nothing.

movevars.description: Moves table variables to a new position, before or after another variable (given by name or number), or to the end.

movmax.description: Moving maximum over a sliding window; options as in movmean.

movmean.description: Moving (rolling, sliding-window) average over windows of k samples centred on each point (for even k, one more sample before than after), or kb before and kf after. Near the ends the window shrinks by default; 'Endpoints' can be 'discard', 'fill' (NaN) or a number. SamplePoints are not supported. Example: movmean([1 2 3 4 5], 3) is [1.5 2 3 4 4.5].

movmedian.description: Moving median over a sliding window, useful for removing spikes; options as in movmean.

movmin.description: Moving minimum over a sliding window; options as in movmean.

movstd.description: Moving standard deviation over a sliding window; w = 1 normalizes by the window size instead of size-1. Other options as in movmean.

movsum.description: Moving sum over a sliding window; windows and options work as in movmean.

movvar.description: Moving variance over a sliding window; options as in movstd.

mrdivide.description: Same as B / A, which solves X*A = B.

mustBeA.description: Validation function: raises an error unless value is of one of the named classes (a class name, or a cell/string array of names; subclasses count).

mustBeFile.description: Validation function: does nothing if the value names an existing file, and raises an error otherwise. Useful in classdef property declarations, e.g. r (1,1) double {mustBeFile}.

mustBeFinite.description: Validation function: does nothing if no element is Inf or NaN, and raises an error otherwise. Useful in classdef property declarations, e.g. r (1,1) double {mustBeFinite}.

mustBeFolder.description: Validation function: does nothing if the value names an existing folder, and raises an error otherwise. Useful in classdef property declarations, e.g. r (1,1) double {mustBeFolder}.

mustBeGreaterThan.description: Validation function: raises an error unless every element of value is greater than c.

mustBeGreaterThanOrEqual.description: Validation function: raises an error unless every element of value is at least c.

mustBeInRange.description: Validation function: raises an error unless every element lies between lower and upper (inclusive).

mustBeInteger.description: Validation function: does nothing if every element is a finite whole number, and raises an error otherwise. Useful in classdef property declarations, e.g. r (1,1) double {mustBeInteger}.

mustBeLessThan.description: Validation function: raises an error unless every element of value is less than c.

mustBeLessThanOrEqual.description: Validation function: raises an error unless every element of value is at most c.

mustBeMember.description: Validation function: raises an error unless value (number, text or cell of text) is one of the allowed values.

mustBeNegative.description: Validation function: does nothing if every element is less than zero, and raises an error otherwise. Useful in classdef property declarations, e.g. r (1,1) double {mustBeNegative}.

mustBeNonNan.description: Validation function: does nothing if no element is NaN, and raises an error otherwise. Useful in classdef property declarations, e.g. r (1,1) double {mustBeNonNan}.

mustBeNonempty.description: Validation function: does nothing if the value is not empty, and raises an error otherwise. Useful in classdef property declarations, e.g. r (1,1) double {mustBeNonempty}.

mustBeNonnegative.description: Validation function: does nothing if every element is zero or greater, and raises an error otherwise. Useful in classdef property declarations, e.g. r (1,1) double {mustBeNonnegative}.

mustBeNonpositive.description: Validation function: does nothing if every element is zero or less, and raises an error otherwise. Useful in classdef property declarations, e.g. r (1,1) double {mustBeNonpositive}.

mustBeNonzero.description: Validation function: does nothing if no element is zero, and raises an error otherwise. Useful in classdef property declarations, e.g. r (1,1) double {mustBeNonzero}.

mustBeNonzeroLengthText.description: Validation function: does nothing if the value is text with at least one character, and raises an error otherwise. Useful in classdef property declarations, e.g. r (1,1) double {mustBeNonzeroLengthText}.

mustBeNumeric.description: Validation function: does nothing if the value is a numeric array, and raises an error otherwise. Useful in classdef property declarations, e.g. r (1,1) double {mustBeNumeric}.

mustBeNumericOrLogical.description: Validation function: does nothing if the value is numeric or logical, and raises an error otherwise. Useful in classdef property declarations, e.g. r (1,1) double {mustBeNumericOrLogical}.

mustBePositive.description: Validation function: does nothing if every element is greater than zero, and raises an error otherwise. Useful in classdef property declarations, e.g. r (1,1) double {mustBePositive}.

mustBeReal.description: Validation function: does nothing if the value has no imaginary part, and raises an error otherwise. Useful in classdef property declarations, e.g. r (1,1) double {mustBeReal}.

mustBeText.description: Validation function: does nothing if the value is a char vector, string, or cell array of char vectors, and raises an error otherwise. Useful in classdef property declarations, e.g. r (1,1) double {mustBeText}.

mustBeTextScalar.description: Validation function: does nothing if the value is one piece of text (char row vector or string scalar), and raises an error otherwise. Useful in classdef property declarations, e.g. r (1,1) double {mustBeTextScalar}.

mustBeVector.description: Validation function: does nothing if the value is a row or column vector, and raises an error otherwise. Useful in classdef property declarations, e.g. r (1,1) double {mustBeVector}.

nan.description: Not-a-Number, the result of undefined operations such as 0/0. n gives an n-by-n result; (m, n) or [m n] gives m-by-n; more sizes such as (m, n, p) give an N-D array. NaN is unequal to everything, itself included; test for it with isnan.

nanmax.description: Maximum that ignores NaN values, like max.

nanmean.description: Mean that ignores NaN values; same as mean(..., 'omitnan').

nanmin.description: Minimum that ignores NaN values, like min.

nanstd.description: Standard deviation that ignores NaN values; flag 1 normalizes by N instead of N-1.

nansum.description: Sum that ignores NaN values; same as sum(..., 'omitnan').

nargin.description: Inside a function, the number of inputs the caller passed. nargin(fname) is not supported.

narginchk.description: Inside a function, throws an error if the number of inputs passed is below minargs or above maxargs.

nargout.description: Inside a function, the number of outputs the caller asked for.

nargoutchk.description: Accepted for compatibility; mylab does not check anything.

nchoosek.description: With scalar n, the number of ways to pick k items from n (the binomial coefficient). With a vector v, every k-element combination of its entries, one per row. Example: nchoosek(5, 2) is 10.

ndgrid.description: Like meshgrid but the first vector runs along dimension 1 (down the rows), the second along dimension 2 and so on: X and Y are numel(x)-by-numel(y).

ndims.description: Number of dimensions of A, never less than 2. Example: ndims(zeros(2, 3, 4)) is 3.

newline.description: A char vector holding the line-feed character (code 10).

nextpow2.description: Smallest integer p with 2^p >= abs(n), element by element; handy for choosing an FFT length. Example: nextpow2(100) is 7.

nexttile.description: Creates the next axes of the current tiled layout and makes it current; nexttile(k) goes to tile k (counting along rows) and [r c] makes an axes spanning r rows and c columns. Without a layout a 'flow' layout is started.

nnz.description: Number of nonzero elements in x.

norm.description: For a vector, the p-norm (sum(abs(v).^p))^(1/p); p defaults to 2, the Euclidean length, and Inf or -Inf give the largest or smallest magnitude. For a matrix, p may be 1, 2 (default, the largest singular value), Inf or 'fro' (Frobenius). Example: norm([3 4]) is 5.

normalize.description: Rescales data along the first dimension whose size is not 1. method is 'zscore' (default; option 'std' or 'robust'), 'range' (to [0 1] or a given [a b]), 'norm' (divide by the p-norm, default 2), 'center' (subtract the mean, the median or a value) or 'scale' (divide by the std, 'mad', 'first', 'iqr' or a value).

normcdf.description: Normal cumulative distribution function: the probability that a value is at most x. Defaults mu = 0, sigma = 1. 'upper' gives the accurate upper tail. Example: normcdf(0) is 0.5.

norminv.description: Inverse of normcdf (normal quantile). Example: norminv(0.975) is about 1.96.

normpdf.description: Normal (Gaussian) probability density at x, with mean mu (default 0) and standard deviation sigma (default 1). Inputs expand against scalars. sigma <= 0 gives NaN.

normrnd.description: Normally distributed random numbers with the given mean and standard deviation, shaped like the parameters or by the size arguments. Uses the generator controlled by rng.

now.description: Current date and time as a serial day number (days counted from year 0), with the time of day as a fraction.

nthargout.description: Calls f with the given inputs and returns only its n-th output. A vector n returns several outputs as a cell array; nout sets how many outputs f is asked for. Example: nthargout(2, @max, [3 9 2]) is 2.

nthroot.description: Real n-th root of each element; for negative x with odd n the real negative root is returned, e.g. nthroot(-8, 3) is -2. Negative x with an even or non-integer n is an error.

null.description: Orthonormal basis for the null space of A: the columns of Z satisfy A*Z = 0.

num2cell.description: Cell array the same size as A, with each element of A in its own cell.
