num2str.description: Converts numbers to text. Integers print in full; other values keep four digits after the decimal point (at least five significant digits for small values), with trailing zeros dropped. precision sets the number of significant digits and format is a sprintf format. Matrices give a char matrix with one row per row. Text input is returned as is. Example: num2str(pi) is '3.1416'.

numel.description: Total number of elements in A, the product of all its dimensions.

ode113.description: Solver for non-stiff problems at tight tolerances. mylab uses a high-order (8th order) Runge-Kutta method instead of a multistep method; options and outputs are as for ode45.

ode15s.description: Solver for stiff problems (implicit backward differentiation formulas). ode23t and ode23tb use the same method and ode23s an implicit Runge-Kutta method. Options and outputs are as for ode45; mass matrices are not supported.

ode23.description: Like ode45 but with a lower-order (2,3) Runge-Kutta pair, which can be cheaper at loose tolerances. Supports the same options and outputs.

ode23s.description: Solver for stiff problems (implicit backward differentiation formulas). ode23t and ode23tb use the same method and ode23s an implicit Runge-Kutta method. Options and outputs are as for ode45; mass matrices are not supported.

ode23t.description: Solver for stiff problems (implicit backward differentiation formulas). ode23t and ode23tb use the same method and ode23s an implicit Runge-Kutta method. Options and outputs are as for ode45; mass matrices are not supported.

ode23tb.description: Solver for stiff problems (implicit backward differentiation formulas). ode23t and ode23tb use the same method and ode23s an implicit Runge-Kutta method. Options and outputs are as for ode45; mass matrices are not supported.

usage: [t, y, te, ye, ie] = ode45(f, tspan, y0, options)
ode45.description: Solves the ODE y' = f(t, y) from y(tspan(1)) = y0 with an explicit Runge-Kutta (4,5) pair. If tspan has two elements, the output holds the solver steps, refined with four points per step taken from the solver's own interpolant; with more elements, the solution at exactly those times. Options from odeset: RelTol (default 1e-3), AbsTol (1e-6), MaxStep, InitialStep, Refine and Events. An event function [value, isterminal, direction] = g(t, y) reports zero crossings of value (direction 1: rising only, -1: falling only, 0: both); te, ye and ie give their times, states and indices, and a terminal event stops the integration. sol is a structure with x, y (and xe, ye, ie) for use with deval.

ode78.description: High-order Runge-Kutta solver for smooth non-stiff problems at tight tolerances. Options and outputs are as for ode45.

ode89.description: High-order Runge-Kutta solver (the same method as ode78 here). Options and outputs are as for ode45.

odeget.description: Reads one option from an odeset structure (the name is not case sensitive), or returns default (or []) when it is not set.

odeset.description: Creates or updates an options structure for the ODE solvers, e.g. odeset('RelTol', 1e-6, 'Events', @myevents).

ones.description: Array filled with 1. With no size it returns the scalar 1; n gives an n-by-n result; (m, n) or [m n] gives m-by-n; more sizes such as (m, n, p) give an N-D array. A class name sets the type.

optimoptions.description: Same as optimset; the solver name is accepted and ignored. Returns a plain struct.

optimset.description: Builds an options struct from name/value pairs for fzero, fminsearch and similar solvers. mylab reads TolX, TolFun, MaxIter and MaxFunEvals where they apply and ignores other names.

or.description: Same as A | B (element-wise logical OR).

orderfields.description: Returns the struct with its fields sorted alphabetically (by character code).

orth.description: Orthonormal basis for the column space (range) of A.

outerjoin.description: Like innerjoin but also keeps rows without a match ('Type' 'full', 'left' or 'right'), filling the missing side with NaN, empty text or <missing>. Without 'MergeKeys' the key variables of both tables are kept (with _left and _right suffixes); with it they are merged into one.

pad.description: Pads text with spaces (or the single character ch) to length n. side is 'right' (default), 'left' or 'both'. Without n, the elements of a cell or string array are padded to the length of the longest one. Text already longer than n is left alone. Example: pad('ab', 5, 'left', '*') is '***ab'.

pagemtimes.description: Matrix multiplication applied page by page: each 2-D slice X(:,:,k) is multiplied by the matching slice Y(:,:,k). The inner dimensions of each pair of pages must agree.

parula.description: n-by-3 matrix of RGB colours (default 256) running from dark blue through green to yellow. mylab uses matplotlib's perceptually uniform 'viridis' map for parula, also the default colormap. Use with colormap, e.g. colormap(parula(16)).

pascal.description: Pascal matrix: P(i, j) is the binomial coefficient (i+j-2 choose j-1), a symmetric positive definite matrix of integers. pascal(n, 1) is a lower-triangular factor with alternating column signs that is its own inverse.

patch.description: Draws a filled polygon with corners (x(k), y(k)); c is a colour name or RGB triplet, and matrix x, y draw one polygon per column. fill replaces the plot unless hold is on; patch always adds to the current axes. Options: FaceColor, EdgeColor, FaceAlpha, LineWidth, DisplayName. Returns a graphics handle when an output is requested (see get and set).

path.description: Current search path as one char vector with folders separated by the system path separator.

pause.description: Waits n seconds (at most an hour). pause with no argument, or with text such as 'on', returns immediately instead of waiting for a key press.

pchip.description: Shape-preserving piecewise cubic Hermite interpolation: no overshoot between data points, and monotone data stay monotone. Returns values at xq or a piecewise polynomial for ppval.

pdist.description: Pairwise distances between the rows of X, returned as a row vector (use squareform to get a matrix). metric: 'euclidean' (default), 'squaredeuclidean', 'seuclidean', 'cityblock', 'chebychev', 'minkowski', 'cosine', 'correlation', 'spearman', 'hamming' or 'jaccard'.

peaks.description: A smooth test surface with several hills and dips, given by a sum of Gaussian bumps. The default grid is 49-by-49 points on [-3, 3]; peaks(n) uses n points, a vector v builds the grid from v, and X, Y give the points directly. Without outputs it draws the surface.

periodogram.description: Power spectral density estimate of a signal vector from its squared FFT magnitude. The window defaults to rectangular, nfft to max(256, next power of 2). For real signals the result is one-sided unless range is 'twosided' or 'centered'. f is in rad/sample, or Hz when fs is given. No plot is drawn.

perms.description: Every ordering of the elements of v, one per row, n! rows in total, starting with the reverse of v. Also works on cell arrays. Limited to 11 elements. Example: perms([1 2]) is [2 1; 1 2].

permute.description: Rearranges the dimensions of A in the given order, a permutation of 1..n. permute(A, [2 1]) is the same as transposing a matrix without conjugation.

pi.description: The ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter, 3.14159..., in double precision.

pie.description: Pie chart of the values in x, each slice proportional to its share of the total. Without labels each slice shows its percentage; labels is a cell or string array of text.

pink.description: n-by-3 colormap of pastel pinks, from dark to white.

pinv.description: Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse, computed from the singular value decomposition. Works for rectangular and singular matrices. A tolerance argument is not supported.

plot.description: Draws 2-D lines. With one input, y is plotted against its index (complex y plots real against imaginary part). A matrix y, or a vector x with a matrix y, draws one line per column. linespec combines a colour (r g b c m y k w), a marker (o + * . x s d ^ v < > p h) and a line style (- -- : -.) in any order, e.g. 'r--o'. Name/Value options: LineWidth, Color, MarkerSize, Marker, LineStyle, DisplayName, MarkerFaceColor, MarkerEdgeColor, Visible. Replaces the current plot unless hold is on; an axes handle as first input draws there. h is a Line handle, or a column array of them when several lines are drawn, so h.LineWidth = 2 restyles the line afterwards. Example: plot(0:0.1:1, (0:0.1:1).^2, 'b-').

plot3.description: Draws a line through 3-D points on 3-D axes (matrices draw one line per column). Accepts the same line options as plot and returns Line handles in the same way.

poisscdf.description: Poisson probability of at most x events with mean lambda. Add 'upper' as the last argument to get the upper tail 1 - P.

poisspdf.description: Poisson probability of exactly x events when the mean count is lambda.

poissrnd.description: Poisson random counts with mean lambda.

pol2cart.description: Converts polar (or cylindrical) coordinates, angle in radians, to Cartesian.

polarplot.description: Plots points given by angle theta (radians) and radius rho on polar axes.

poly.description: Polynomial coefficients from a vector of roots r, or the characteristic polynomial of a square matrix A. Example: poly([1 2]) is [1 -3 2].

polyder.description: Coefficients of the derivative of a polynomial. The product and quotient forms with two inputs are not supported.

polyfit.description: Least-squares polynomial of degree n through the points (x, y), highest power first. S holds the triangular factor R, the degrees of freedom df, the residual norm normr and rsquared, for error estimates with polyval. With mu, x is first centred and scaled: the fit uses (x - mu(1)) / mu(2), where mu = [mean(x); std(x)]; this helps with large or badly scaled x.

polyint.description: Coefficients of the antiderivative of a polynomial, with constant of integration k (default 0).

polyval.description: Evaluates the polynomial p (highest power first) at each element of x. With mu from polyfit, x is centred and scaled first. With S from polyfit, delta is an error estimate such that y +/- delta covers new observations about 68% of the time for normal errors.

pow2db.description: Converts power ratio to decibels: 10*log10(p). Negative values are an error.

ppval.description: Evaluates a piecewise polynomial (from spline, pchip, makima or mkpp) at xq. Points outside the breaks use the first or last piece.

prctile.description: Percentiles of the data for percentages p (0..100), along the first dimension whose size is not 1 or along dim; NaN values are ignored. Sorted values are treated as sitting at percentages 100*(i-0.5)/n with linear interpolation between them. Example: prctile([1 2 3 4], 50) is 2.5.

primes.description: Row vector of all prime numbers less than or equal to n. Example: primes(10) is [2 3 5 7].

print.description: Saves the current figure (or figure fig, a handle or number, or -fN) to a file. A -d option such as -dpng, -djpeg, -dpdf, -dsvg or -depsc picks the format when the file name has no extension; PNG is the default. -rN sets the resolution in dots per inch (default 150). Renderer options such as -painters are ignored. The .fig format is not supported.

prod.description: Product of elements, working along the first dimension whose size is not 1 unless dim or 'all' is given. 'omitnan' skips NaN values. prod([]) is 1.

profile.description: Accepted for compatibility; no profiling is done.

properties.description: Lists the public properties of an object or class; with an output, returns them as a cell column.

psi.description: Digamma function, the derivative of gammaln. psi(k, x) gives the k-th derivative of digamma (polygamma), for non-negative integer k.

pwd.description: Current working folder as a char vector.

usage: [pxx, f] = pwelch(x, window, noverlap, nfft, fs)
pwelch.description: Welch power spectral density estimate: averages windowed periodograms of overlapping segments, giving a smoother spectrum than periodogram. Defaults: Hamming window of about length/4.5 samples, 50% overlap, nfft max(256, next power of 2). window may be a length or a vector. One-sided for real signals; no plot is drawn.

qr.description: QR factorization A = Q*R with Q orthogonal and R upper triangular. Any second argument (such as 0 or 'econ') gives the economy-size version. Column pivoting is not supported.

quad.description: Older names for numerical integration; in mylab quad, quadgk and quadl all behave exactly like integral, including the 'AbsTol' and 'RelTol' options. A positional tolerance argument is ignored.

quadgk.description: Older names for numerical integration; in mylab quad, quadgk and quadl all behave exactly like integral, including the 'AbsTol' and 'RelTol' options. A positional tolerance argument is ignored.

quadl.description: Older names for numerical integration; in mylab quad, quadgk and quadl all behave exactly like integral, including the 'AbsTol' and 'RelTol' options. A positional tolerance argument is ignored.

usage: x = quadprog(H, f, A, b, Aeq, beq, lb, ub)
x = quadprog(H, f, A, b, Aeq, beq, lb, ub, x0)
quadprog.description: Quadratic programming: minimizes 0.5*x'*H*x + f'*x subject to linear constraints and bounds. Without constraints and with H positive definite the minimum is solved directly; otherwise a sequential quadratic programming method is used, which finds a local minimum. Options are ignored.

quantile.description: Quantiles for probabilities p (0..1), computed the same way as prctile.

quit.description: Ends the mylab session, optionally with a numeric exit status for the operating system.

quiver.description: Draws arrows with components (U, V) starting at the points (X, Y), or on a grid of indices. Arrows are scaled automatically to fit between grid points; scale multiplies that factor and 0 turns scaling off ('AutoScale', 'off' does the same).

rad2deg.description: Converts angles from radians to degrees (multiplies by 180/pi).

rand.description: Uniform random numbers from 0 up to (not including) 1. n gives an n-by-n result; (m, n) or [m n] gives m-by-n; more sizes such as (m, n, p) give an N-D array. Values come from the session's generator, which rng can seed; the stream differs from other implementations even with the same seed.

randi.description: Random integers drawn uniformly from 1..imax, or from imin..imax when a two-element range is given. The result is of class double. Example: randi(6, 1, 3) simulates three dice.

randn.description: Normally distributed random numbers with mean 0 and standard deviation 1. n gives an n-by-n result; (m, n) or [m n] gives m-by-n; more sizes such as (m, n, p) give an N-D array. Uses the generator controlled by rng.

randperm.description: Row vector holding a random ordering of the integers 1..n. With k, only the first k entries of such an ordering are returned, so they are distinct.

randsample.description: Random sample of k values from 1..n or from the elements of a population vector, without replacement unless replace is true. Weights w make the draw weighted (and with replacement unless replace is given as false). Uses the generator controlled by rng.

range.description: max minus min along the first dimension whose size is not 1, or along dim.

rank.description: Number of linearly independent rows or columns, estimated from the singular values. A tolerance argument is not supported.

usage: [p, h, stats] = ranksum(x, y, Name, Value)
ranksum.description: Wilcoxon rank sum test (equivalent to the Mann-Whitney U test), a non-parametric test that two samples have equal medians. Two-sided only. Uses the exact distribution for small samples without ties and a normal approximation otherwise ('method' 'exact' or 'approximate' overrides). 'alpha' sets the level for h.

rdivide.description: Same as A ./ B (element-wise right division).

readcell.description: Reads a delimited text file into a cell array: numeric fields become numbers, other fields char vectors and empty fields <missing>.

readlines.description: Reads a text file into a string column, one element per line (a final line break does not add an empty line).

readmatrix.description: Reads delimited numeric text into a matrix. The delimiter (comma, tab, semicolon, bar or whitespace) is detected when not given. Leading lines with only text, such as a header row, are skipped automatically unless 'NumHeaderLines' says how many to skip. Empty or non-numeric fields become NaN, and short rows are padded with NaN.

readtable.description: Reads a delimited text file (CSV, tab, semicolon...) into a table. The first row gives the variable names; all-numeric columns become numbers (blank cells become NaN), other columns become cell arrays of text (or strings with 'TextType', 'string').

realmin.description: Smallest positive normalized double-precision number, about 2.2251e-308.

rectwin.description: Rectangular window: a column of n ones.

refresh.description: Updates figure windows so that pending drawing appears, e.g. inside an animation loop. shg and refresh do the same.

usage: [st, en, te, mat, tok, nm, sp] = regexp(s, expr)
regexp.description: Regular-expression search. Keywords 'match', 'tokens', 'names', 'start', 'end' and 'split' choose which results are returned, in the order given; without them the outputs are start indices, end indices, token extents (always empty in mylab), matches, tokens, named tokens and split pieces. 'once' returns only the first match, not wrapped in a cell. Named groups are written (?<name>...); 'names' gives a 1-by-N struct array with one element per match (a scalar struct with 'once'). Matching uses Python's regex engine, so rare constructs may differ. A cell array s gives a cell of results.

regexpi.description: Case-insensitive form of regexp: the same outputs and options, but letters match regardless of case.

regexprep.description: Replaces every match of a regular expression. In the replacement, $1, $2, ... insert captured groups and $0 the whole match. 'once' replaces only the first match. s may be a cell array or string array. Example: regexprep('abc', '(b)', '[$1]') is 'a[b]c'.

usage: [b, bint, r, rint, stats] = regress(y, X)
regress.description: Multiple linear regression by least squares: finds b so that X*b best fits y. Include a column of ones in X to fit an intercept. bint gives 100*(1-alpha)% confidence intervals for b, r the residuals, rint residual intervals and stats = [R^2, F, p-value, error variance]. Rows containing NaN are ignored. Example: b = regress(y, [ones(size(x)) x]) fits a line.

rem.description: Remainder after division, defined as a - fix(a./b).*b, so a nonzero result has the sign of a. rem(a, 0) is NaN. Example: rem(-1, 3) is -1.

removevars.description: Removes the named (or numbered) variables from a table.

repelem.description: Repeats elements. For a vector v, each element is repeated n times (n may be a vector with one count per element). For a matrix, each row is repeated r times and each column c times. Example: repelem([1 2], [2 3]) is [1 1 2 2 2].

replace.description: Replaces every occurrence of the literal text old with new (no regular expressions). old may list several patterns, with new either one replacement for all or one per pattern; longer patterns win where they overlap. s may be a char vector, a string, a string array or a cell array of text; string input gives string output.

repmat.description: Tiles A m times vertically and n times horizontally (n times both ways for a single n); further counts repeat it along higher dimensions. Works with numeric, logical, char, cell and struct arrays. Example: repmat([1 2], 2, 2) is [1 2 1 2; 1 2 1 2].

usage: y = resample(x, p, q, n, beta)
resample.description: Changes the sample rate by the factor p/q, with an anti-aliasing low-pass FIR filter (Kaiser window; n sets its length, beta its shape). Works along a row vector or down columns.

rescale.description: Linearly maps the smallest element of x to l (default 0) and the largest to u (default 1), using all elements. InputMin and InputMax set the source range, clipping values outside it. Constant data maps to l.

reshape.description: Rearranges the elements of A into an array of the given size, reading and writing in column-major order. One size may be given as [] and is computed from the element count, which must not change. Works on cells and structs too. Example: reshape(1:6, 2, 3) is [1 3 5; 2 4 6].

rethrow.description: Throws again an error caught with try/catch; err is a struct with message and identifier fields, such as the variable from catch err.

reverse.description: Reverses the order of the characters. Example: reverse('abc') is 'cba'.

rmdir.description: Removes an empty folder, or with 's' the folder and everything in it. With outputs, failure is reported through status and msg instead of an error.

rmfield.description: Returns a copy of the struct without the named field(s). Naming a missing field is an error.

rmmissing.description: Removes missing entries: NaN in numeric data, empty char vectors in cell arrays, <missing> strings. A vector loses the missing elements, a matrix or table the rows (or columns, with dim 2) that contain at least n missing values (default 1). TF marks what was removed.

rmpath.description: Removes folders from the search path.

rng.description: Resets the random number generator used by rand, randn, randi and randperm. A numeric seed gives a repeatable stream, 'default' is the same as seed 0, and 'shuffle' reseeds from the operating system. Returns nothing; saving and restoring a generator state is not supported.

roots.description: Roots of the polynomial with coefficients p, as a column vector (possibly complex).

rot90.description: Rotates a matrix by 90 degrees counter-clockwise, k times (negative k rotates clockwise). Example: rot90([1 2; 3 4]) is [2 4; 1 3].

round.description: Rounds to the nearest integer, with halves going away from zero (round(2.5) is 3, round(-2.5) is -3). With n, rounds to n digits after the decimal point; negative n rounds to tens, hundreds and so on. Integer-class input is returned unchanged.

rows2vars.description: Transposes a numeric table: each original row becomes a variable, and a first variable OriginalVariableNames lists the old column names.

run.description: Runs a script file (with or without the .m extension) in the current workspace, so its variables stay available afterwards. The script's folder is added to the search path.

save.description: Writes variables from the workspace to a .mat file (the extension is added if missing; the default name is matlab.mat). Only numeric, logical, char and string variables are saved; cells, structs and handles are skipped. Option flags such as -ascii are ignored.

saveas.description: Saves a figure, given as a handle (e.g. gcf) or a figure number, as an image file at 150 dpi. The type comes from the file extension (png, pdf, svg, jpg, eps, tif) or from format when the name has no extension. The .fig format is not supported and gives an error.

sawtooth.description: Sawtooth wave with period 2*pi running between -1 and 1. width (0..1, default 1) sets where in the period the peak is; 0.5 gives a triangle wave.

scatter.description: Draws a marker at each point (x, y). sz is the marker area (default 36), scalar or per point; c is a colour name, an RGB triplet or one value per point mapped through the colormap. Markers are hollow unless 'filled' is given. Options: DisplayName, MarkerFaceColor, MarkerEdgeColor, LineWidth, MarkerFaceAlpha. s is a Scatter handle with properties such as XData, YData, SizeData and CData.

scatter3.description: Draws a marker at each 3-D point (x, y, z) on 3-D axes.

semilogx.description: Like plot, but with a logarithmic x axis.

semilogy.description: Like plot, but with a logarithmic y axis.

set.description: Changes properties of graphics handles, e.g. set(h, 'LineWidth', 2, 'Color', 'r'). If h holds several handles each one is changed. A struct s of property values is also accepted. set(0, 'DefaultLineLineWidth', w) and a few other root defaults change later plots. Dot assignment, e.g. h.LineWidth = 2, does the same for one property; on an array of handles it changes all of them, and reading a property from an array gives a cell array.

setdiff.description: Values in a that are not in b, without repeats, sorted unless 'stable' is given; c = a(ia). Accepts cell arrays of text. The 'rows' option is ignored.

setfield.description: Returns a copy of the struct with the field set to value, the same as s.(name) = value. Only a single field level is supported.

setxor.description: Values found in exactly one of a and b, without repeats, sorted unless 'stable' is given. Accepts cell arrays of text. The 'rows' option is ignored.

sgolayfilt.description: Savitzky-Golay smoothing filter: fits a polynomial of the given order to each window of framelen samples (odd, larger than order). Weights are not supported.

sgtitle.description: Sets one title for the whole figure, above all subplots. suptitle does the same.

shading.description: Sets how surfaces are drawn: 'faceted' (the default) outlines each patch, 'flat' and 'interp' hide the grid lines. Applies to the surfaces in the current axes and to later surf calls. mylab draws 'interp' like 'flat' with smoothing.

shg.description: Updates figure windows so that pending drawing appears, e.g. inside an animation loop. shg and refresh do the same.

sign.description: -1, 0 or 1 according to the sign of each element. For complex x, returns x./abs(x) (0 where x is 0).

sin.description: Sine of each element, with x in radians.

sinc.description: Normalized sinc function sin(pi*x)./(pi*x), with sinc(0) = 1.

sind.description: Sine of angles given in degrees. Multiples of 180 give exactly 0.

single.description: Converts to single precision (32-bit floating point).

size.description: Dimensions of A. With one output, a row vector holding the length of every dimension; size(A, dim) gives one length (1 for a dimension beyond ndims(A)) and a vector of dims gives several. With several outputs, the last output absorbs all remaining dimensions (their product), so [r, c] = size(A) puts the product of dimensions 2 and up in c. Example: size(ones(2, 5, 3)) is [2 5 3].

skewness.description: Sample skewness, a measure of asymmetry (0 for symmetric data). flag 1 (default) gives the plain moment estimate, flag 0 the bias-corrected one. NaN values are ignored.

smoothdata.description: Smooths noisy data along the first dimension whose size is not 1. method is 'movmean' (default), 'movmedian', 'gaussian' or 'sgolay' (Savitzky-Golay with polynomial degree d, default 2); the lowess/loess methods are not supported. Without a window, about a tenth of the data length is used, which may differ from other implementations. NaN values are ignored by default.

sort.description: Sorts in ascending order (or 'descend') along the first dimension whose size is not 1, or along dim. idx holds the original positions. Equal values keep their order; NaN goes last when ascending and first when descending; complex values sort by magnitude. Cell arrays of char vectors and string arrays are sorted alphabetically (by character code). Example: sort([3 1 2]) is [1 2 3].

sortrows.description: Sorts the rows of a matrix, char array or cell array. Rows are compared by the listed columns in turn (by default all columns, left to right); a negative column number sorts that column in descending order. Cell array columns must hold text or numeric scalars. Ties keep their original order. idx is the row permutation. Example: sortrows([3 1; 1 2; 3 0], [1 -2]) is [1 2; 3 1; 3 0].

usage: S = sparse(i, j, v, m, n)
sparse.description: Accepted for compatibility but always produces an ordinary dense matrix. sparse(m, n) is an m-by-n zero matrix; sparse(i, j, v, ...) places v(k) at row i(k), column j(k), adding up values that land on the same position.

sph2cart.description: Converts spherical coordinates (azimuth, elevation in radians, radius) to Cartesian.

spline.description: Cubic spline through the points (x, y) with not-a-knot end conditions; if y has two more values than x, the first and last give the end slopes. With xq, returns the values there; otherwise returns a piecewise polynomial for ppval. If y is a matrix, each row is a component of a vector-valued spline.

split.description: Splits text at whitespace, or at a delimiter (a cell or string array lists several). Runs of delimiters count as one break unless 'CollapseDelimiters' is false. One input text gives a column of pieces (a cell of char vectors, or a string array for string input); a cell array whose elements all split into the same number of pieces gives a matrix. Example: split("a,b", ",") is ["a"; "b"].

splitapply.description: Splits the data into groups given by the group numbers G (from findgroups), calls f on each group and stacks the results, one row per group. Matrices are split by rows. f must return the same size for each group; return a cell such as @(x) {x} for anything else. Example: splitapply(@sum, [1 2 3], [1 2 1]) is [4 2].

splitlines.description: Splits text at line breaks (\n, \r\n or \r). A string gives a string column; a char vector gives a cell column of char vectors.

spring.description: n-by-3 colormap from magenta to yellow.

sprintf.description: Formats data into text using % conversions (%d, %i, %u, %f, %e, %g, %x, %o, %c, %s, %%) with optional flags, width and precision (a * takes them from the data). Escapes such as \n and \t are expanded. Array arguments are taken element by element and the format is reused until all data is consumed. A non-integer given to %d is shown in %e style; an integer given to %s is taken as a character code, so sprintf('%s', 65) is 'A'. Returns a char vector, or a string if fmt is a string. Example: sprintf('%d-%d', 1, 2) is '1-2'.

sqrt.description: Square root of each element. Negative inputs give complex results, e.g. sqrt(-4) is 0 + 2i. Integer inputs are converted to double first.

sqrtm.description: Matrix square root: Y*Y equals A. Not the same as the element-wise sqrt.

square.description: Square wave with period 2*pi taking the values +1 and -1; duty is the percentage of each period spent at +1 (default 50).

squareform.description: Converts between the vector of pairwise distances returned by pdist and the full symmetric distance matrix with zeros on the diagonal.

squeeze.description: Removes dimensions of length 1 from A. The result always keeps at least two dimensions, so 2-D inputs, including row vectors, are returned unchanged. Example: squeeze(ones(1, 1, 3)) is a 3-by-1 column.

sscanf.description: Reads values from text according to a format, the reverse of sprintf. Supports %d, %i, %u, %o, %x, %f, %e, %g, %s, %c and %[...] with optional field width and * to skip a field; the format repeats until the text is used up or does not match. Numbers come back as a column; if everything read is text the result is a char row. sz (n, Inf or [m n]) shapes the output, filling columns first. count is the number of fields read; next is always one past the end. Example: sscanf('3 4 5', '%d') is [3; 4; 5].

stairs.description: Draws y as a staircase that holds each value until the next x. Returns a graphics handle when an output is requested (see get and set).

startsWith.description: True if s begins with pattern (or any pattern in a cell array). Works element-wise on a cell array s.

std.description: Standard deviation along the first dimension whose size is not 1, or along dim. w = 0 (the default, also used when w is []) divides by N-1; w = 1 divides by N. A single value gives 0. 'omitnan' ignores NaN. Example: std([2 4 4 4 5 5 7 9], 1) is 2.

stem.description: Plots each value as a vertical stem from zero topped with a marker, as for discrete signals. Returns a graphics handle when an output is requested (see get and set).

str2double.description: Converts text to a double. Returns NaN when the text is not a number. Cell arrays and string arrays are converted element by element (a <missing> string gives NaN); a numeric input gives NaN. Example: str2double(["1.5" "x"]) is [1.5 NaN].

str2func.description: Makes a function handle from a name such as 'sin' or from anonymous-function text such as '@(x) x + 1'.

str2num.description: Evaluates text as a bracketed expression, so '1 2 3' gives [1 2 3] and '[1;2]' a column. On failure returns [] and ok is false. Because the text is executed, prefer str2double for untrusted input.

strcat.description: Concatenates texts horizontally. Trailing whitespace of char inputs is removed first; strings keep theirs. If any input is a cell array the result is a cell array, joined element by element. Example: strcat('a ', 'b') is 'ab'.

strcmp.description: True if two texts are identical (case-sensitive). Either input may be a cell array or string array, giving an element-wise logical array. Non-text inputs give false rather than an error.

strcmpi.description: Like strcmp but ignores upper/lower case.

strfind.description: Starting indices of every occurrence of pattern in s, overlapping ones included, as a row vector ([] if none). For a cell array, returns a cell of index vectors. Example: strfind('abcabc', 'bc') is [2 5].

string.description: Converts to string. A char row becomes a string scalar; a char matrix gives one string per row; a cell array of text gives a string array of the same size; numbers are converted element by element to their short text form, with NaN becoming <missing>. string() is the empty string "". Example: string([1 2]) is ["1" "2"].

strings.description: Creates a string array of the given size filled with empty strings "". strings(1, 1) is the empty string scalar.

strip.description: Removes leading and trailing whitespace, or the single character ch. side is 'both' (default), 'left' or 'right'. s may be a char vector, a string, a string array or a cell array of text; string input gives string output.

strjoin.description: Joins the texts in a cell array or string array into one piece of text, separated by delimiter (a space by default). Escapes such as '\n' in the delimiter are expanded. Returns a char vector for cell input and a string for string input.

strjust.description: Moves the text in each row of a char matrix to the 'right' (default), 'left' or 'center', keeping the width. Only char arrays are accepted; strings and cell arrays are an error.

strlength.description: Number of characters in a char vector or string scalar. For a string array or cell array of text, an array of lengths of the same size (NaN for <missing>).

strncmp.description: True if the first n characters of two texts match (case-sensitive). Texts shorter than n never match. Cell arrays compare element by element.

strncmpi.description: Like strncmp but ignores upper/lower case.

strrep.description: Replaces every occurrence of old in s with new. s may be a cell array or string array. Example: strrep('a-b-c', '-', '+') is 'a+b+c'.

strsplit.description: Splits text at a delimiter (default: whitespace) or at any of a cell array of delimiters, which may contain escapes such as '\t'. Runs of consecutive delimiters count as one unless 'CollapseDelimiters' is false. A string input gives a string row; a char input gives a cell row. matches holds the delimiter text that was found. Example: strsplit('a,,b', ',') is {'a', 'b'}; with 'CollapseDelimiters', false it is {'a', '', 'b'}.

strtok.description: First token of the text: leading delimiter characters (default: whitespace) are skipped and the token runs up to the next delimiter. rest is the remainder, starting at that delimiter. Works elementwise on cell and string arrays. Example: [t, r] = strtok('  red green') gives t = 'red' and r = ' green'.

strtrim.description: Removes leading and trailing whitespace (and null characters). Works on char arrays, strings, string arrays and cell arrays of text.

struct.description: Creates a struct from field name/value pairs. A value that is a cell array creates a struct array the size of that cell, one element per cell; wrap a cell in another cell, e.g. {{1, 2}}, to store it as a single field value. Example: s = struct('x', 1, 'y', 'hi').

struct2cell.description: Column cell array holding the field values of a scalar struct, in field order.

struct2table.description: Converts a struct array (one row per element) or a scalar struct of column vectors into a table whose variables are the struct fields.

structfun.description: Calls f on the value of each field of a scalar struct. By default the scalar results form a column vector; with 'UniformOutput' false the results are returned as a struct with the same field names.

strvcat.description: Stacks texts as rows of a char matrix padded with spaces. Empty inputs are skipped.

sub2ind.description: Converts subscripts into linear indices for an array of size sz (column-major numbering). Subscript arrays must have matching sizes; scalars are expanded. With fewer subscripts than dimensions the last one spans the remaining dimensions. Out-of-range subscripts are an error. Example: sub2ind([3 4], 2, 3) is 8.

subplot.description: Splits the figure into an m-by-n grid of axes and makes axes p current, counting along rows from the top left. A vector p makes one axes spanning those cells. subplot(221) is shorthand for subplot(2, 2, 1). Asking again for the same cell reuses its axes. ax is an Axes handle; subplot(ax) makes it current. See also tiledlayout.

subtitle.description: Adds a smaller second line of text under the title of the current axes. title(txt, subtxt) sets both at once.

sum.description: Sum of elements. For a vector, the total; for a matrix, a row of column sums. dim = 1 sums down columns, dim = 2 across rows, and 'all' sums everything. 'omitnan' skips NaN values. sum([]) is 0. Integer inputs keep their class and saturate. Example: sum([1 2; 3 4]) is [4 6].

summary.description: Prints a short description of each table variable: its size and type, plus the minimum, median and maximum of numeric variables.

summer.description: n-by-3 colormap from green to yellow.

suptitle.description: Sets one title for the whole figure, above all subplots. suptitle does the same.

surf.description: Draws a coloured 3-D surface with heights Z over the grid X, Y (vectors are expanded to a grid; without them the indices are used), coloured with the current colormap. It replaces the current axes (other subplots are kept) unless hold is on. Edges follow the shading setting; options EdgeColor, FaceColor and FaceAlpha are honoured. s is a Surface handle. surfc currently draws the same plot without the contour lines underneath.

surfc.description: Draws a coloured 3-D surface with heights Z over the grid X, Y (vectors are expanded to a grid; without them the indices are used), coloured with the current colormap. It replaces the current axes (other subplots are kept) unless hold is on. Edges follow the shading setting; options EdgeColor, FaceColor and FaceAlpha are honoured. s is a Surface handle. surfc currently draws the same plot without the contour lines underneath.

svd.description: Singular value decomposition A = U*S*V'. With one output, the singular values as a column in decreasing order. Passing any second argument (such as 'econ' or 0) gives the economy-size factors.

table.description: Creates a table: columns (variables) of equal height that may hold numbers, logicals, text in cells or strings. Variables are named after the input variables, or Var1, Var2, ... Rows can be named with 'RowNames' (or later through T.Properties.RowNames) and then indexed by name, as in T('row2', :). Access a variable with T.name, a sub-table with T(rows, vars) and the contents with T{rows, vars}, which can also be assigned.

table2array.description: Concatenates all table variables side by side into one array. The variables must have compatible types.

table2cell.description: Cell array with one cell per table entry: numbers as numeric values, text as char vectors or strings.

table2struct.description: Converts a table into an n-by-1 struct array, one element per row.

tabulate.description: Frequency table of the values in x with columns Value, Count and Percent. For positive integers every value from 1 to max(x) is listed; text in a cell array gives a cell result. Without an output the table is printed.

tail.description: Last k rows of a table or array (default 8).

tan.description: Tangent of each element, with x in radians.

tand.description: Tangent of angles given in degrees; 0 and multiples of 180 give exactly 0.

tcdf.description: Student's t cumulative probability with nu degrees of freedom. Add 'upper' as the last argument to get the upper tail 1 - P.

tempdir.description: The system folder for temporary files, ending with a file separator.

tempname.description: A unique name for a temporary file or folder (nothing is created).

text.description: Writes text on the current axes starting at data point (x, y), vertically centred on it. Vector x, y with a cell array of strings write several labels. Options: FontSize, Color, FontWeight, HorizontalAlignment, VerticalAlignment, Rotation. Returns Text handle(s) on request.

textscan.description: Reads columns of formatted text into a 1-by-n cell array, one cell per conversion: %f and %n give double columns, %d and %u integer columns (int32/uint32, or with a size suffix such as %d8), %s and %q cell columns of text (%q removes double quotes) and %c characters; %*s skips a field. Fields are separated by whitespace or by 'Delimiter'; 'HeaderLines' skips lines first and N limits the number of records. Other options: 'MultipleDelimsAsOne', 'CollectOutput', 'CommentStyle', 'EmptyValue' and 'TextType'.

throw.description: Throws the error described by ME, a struct with message and identifier fields such as one made by MException.

tic.description: Starts a stopwatch. With an output, also returns a start-time value that can be passed to toc.

tiledlayout.description: Starts a grid of axes in the current figure (clearing it). An m-by-n layout has fixed tiles; 'flow' grows and rearranges the grid as tiles are added ('vertical' and 'horizontal' stack them). Use nexttile to create each axes. title(t, txt), xlabel(t, txt) and ylabel(t, txt) label the whole layout. TileSpacing and Padding accept 'loose', 'compact', 'tight' or 'none'.

timeit.description: Measures how long the function handle f (taking no inputs) takes to run: calls it several times and returns the median time in seconds. numOutputs is the number of outputs to request on each call (default 0).

tinv.description: Inverse of tcdf (t quantile), used for confidence intervals. Example: tinv(0.975, 10) is about 2.228.

title.description: Sets the title of the current axes (or of an axes or tiledlayout handle). A cell array or multi-row char array gives several lines, and subtxt adds a subtitle. Options: FontSize, FontWeight, Color, FontName, Interpreter (remembered only). t is a Text handle whose String, FontSize, Color, ... can be changed.

toc.description: Seconds since the last tic (or since tic returned t). Without an output it prints 'Elapsed time is ... seconds.'

toeplitz.description: Toeplitz matrix, constant along each diagonal, with first column c and first row r. With one input the matrix is symmetric. Example: toeplitz([1 2 3]) is [1 2 3; 2 1 2; 3 2 1].

tpdf.description: Student's t density with nu degrees of freedom.

trace.description: Sum of the main diagonal of a square matrix.

transpose.description: Same as A.' : swaps rows and columns without conjugating.

trapz.description: Approximate integral of sampled data by the trapezoid rule, with unit spacing or the points in x. Works along the first dimension whose size is not 1; a dim argument is not supported. Example: trapz([1 2 3]) is 4.

tril.description: Lower triangular part of A: entries above the k-th diagonal are set to zero.

triu.description: Upper triangular part of A: entries below the k-th diagonal are set to zero (k = 0 is the main diagonal).

true.description: Logical 1, or a logical array of ones. n gives an n-by-n result; (m, n) or [m n] gives m-by-n; more sizes such as (m, n, p) give an N-D array.

usage: [h, p, ci, stats] = ttest(..., Name, Value)
ttest.description: One-sample t-test that the data have mean m (default 0), or paired t-test on x - y when y has the same size. h = 1 rejects the hypothesis at the significance level 'Alpha' (default 0.05). 'Tail' is 'both' (default), 'right' or 'left'; 'Dim' picks the dimension. ci is the confidence interval for the mean and stats holds tstat, df and sd. NaN values are ignored.

usage: [h, p, ci, stats] = ttest2(x, y, Name, Value)
ttest2.description: Two-sample t-test that x and y come from populations with equal means. Assumes equal variances unless 'Vartype' is 'unequal' (Welch's test). 'Alpha', 'Tail' and 'Dim' work as in ttest; ci is the interval for the difference of means.

turbo.description: n-by-3 rainbow colormap with smoother brightness than jet.

type.description: Prints the contents of a text file. If the file is not found as given, name.m and the search path are tried.

typecast.description: Reinterprets the bytes of a real numeric scalar or vector as another numeric type ('double', 'single' or an integer class) without changing the bits, using little-endian byte order. The total byte count must divide evenly into the new type. The result is a row, or a column for column input. Example: typecast(single(1), 'uint32') is 1065353216.

uint16.description: Converts to the uint16 integer class: values are rounded to the nearest integer (halves away from zero), clipped to the range 0..65535, and NaN becomes 0. Example: uint16(2.5) is 3.

uint32.description: Converts to the uint32 integer class: values are rounded to the nearest integer (halves away from zero), clipped to the range 0..4294967295, and NaN becomes 0. Example: uint32(2.5) is 3.

uint64.description: Converts to the uint64 integer class: values are rounded to the nearest integer (halves away from zero), clipped to the range 0..about 1.8e19, and NaN becomes 0. Example: uint64(2.5) is 3.

uint8.description: Converts to the uint8 integer class: values are rounded to the nearest integer (halves away from zero), clipped to the range 0..255, and NaN becomes 0. Example: uint8(2.5) is 3.

unifcdf.description: Cumulative probability of the uniform distribution on [a, b] (default [0, 1]). Add 'upper' as the last argument to get the upper tail 1 - P.

unifpdf.description: Density of the continuous uniform distribution on [a, b] (default [0, 1]).

union.description: Values found in a or b, without repeats, sorted unless 'stable' is given. The result is a row unless a is a column. Also accepts cell arrays of text. In mylab ia and ib list the position in a (and in b) of each result value found there. The 'rows' option is ignored.

unique.description: The distinct values of x, sorted unless 'stable' is given (first-appearance order). The result is a row if x is a row, otherwise a column. ia and ic are index columns with u = x(ia) and x = u(ic); 'last' makes ia point to last occurrences. 'rows' finds distinct rows. Also works on cell arrays of char vectors and on string arrays. Example: unique([3 1 3 2]) is [1 2 3].

unmkpp.description: Takes a piecewise polynomial apart: its breaks, coefficient matrix, number of pieces l, order k and number of components d.

unwrap.description: Removes jumps larger than tol (default pi) from phase angles in radians by adding multiples of 2*pi, giving a continuous phase curve.

upper.description: Converts text to upper case, character by character, so the length never changes (a letter whose upper-case form is longer, such as the German sharp s, is kept). Works on char arrays, strings, string arrays and cells.

usage: validateattributes(A, classes, attributes, funcname, varname, argindex)
validateattributes.description: Checks an input and throws a descriptive error if it fails. classes is a cell array of allowed class names (or {} for any; 'numeric', 'float' and 'integer' work as groups). attributes is a cell array of tests such as 'scalar', 'vector', 'row', 'column', '2d', 'square', 'nonempty', 'real', 'finite', 'nonnan', 'integer', 'positive', 'nonnegative', 'nonzero', 'binary', 'even', 'odd', 'increasing', 'nondecreasing', or pairs like '>', 0 / 'numel', 3 / 'size', [NaN 2] (NaN = any). funcname, varname and argindex are optional and only shape the message.

validatestring.description: Matches str against a list of allowed texts, ignoring case and accepting an unambiguous leading part, and returns the full matching option. No match or an ambiguous match is an error. Example: validatestring('lin', {'linear', 'cubic'}) is 'linear'.

vander.description: Vandermonde matrix: column j holds v raised to the power n-j, so the last column is all ones.

var.description: Variance, the square of std. w = 0 (default) divides by N-1 and w = 1 divides by N. Works along the first dimension whose size is not 1 unless dim is given.

varfun.description: Applies the function f to each table variable. Result variables are named like mean_Height. With 'GroupingVariables', f is applied to each group of rows separately and the result has one row per group, with the group values and a GroupCount column. 'OutputFormat' 'uniform' returns a numeric row and 'cell' a cell row instead of a table.

vecnorm.description: p-norm (default 2, the Euclidean length) of each column of A, or of each vector along dim; a vector input gives a single norm. p = Inf gives the largest magnitude. Example: vecnorm([3 0; 4 1]) is [5 1].

ver.description: Prints the versions of mylab, Python and NumPy.

vertcat.description: Stacks arrays on top of each other, the same as [A; B; ...]. They must have the same number of columns.

view.description: Sets the viewing angle of the current 3-D axes: azimuth az and elevation el in degrees. view(2) looks straight down. Has no effect on 2-D axes.

warning.description: Prints a warning message and carries on. warning('off') or warning('off', 'all') silences all warnings and warning('on') restores them; turning off a single identifier is accepted but has no effect.

who.description: Lists the names of the variables in the current workspace, or returns them as a column cell array.

whos.description: Prints a table of the current variables with their sizes, byte counts and classes. Byte counts are reported for numeric, logical and char arrays only.

width.description: Number of variables (columns) of a table.

winter.description: n-by-3 colormap from blue to green.

wrapTo180.description: Wraps angles in degrees into [-180, 180]; values already in range are kept.

wrapTo2Pi.description: Wraps angles in radians into [0, 2*pi]; positive multiples of 2*pi map to 2*pi.

wrapTo360.description: Wraps angles in degrees into [0, 360]; positive multiples of 360 map to 360.

wrapToPi.description: Wraps angles in radians into [-pi, pi]; values already in range are kept.

writecell.description: Writes a cell array of numbers and text to a delimited text file, one row of the cell array per line.

writelines.description: Writes text (a string array, cell array or char vector) to a file, one element per line, each followed by a line break.

writematrix.description: Writes a matrix to a delimited text file with full precision, one row per line. The delimiter may be 'comma' (default; tab for .tsv files), 'tab', 'space', 'semi', 'bar' or any single character. Cell arrays, strings and char arrays are written as text, quoted when they contain the delimiter.

writetable.description: Writes a table to a delimited text file with a header row of variable names.

xcorr.description: Cross-correlation of two vectors (autocorrelation with one input) at every lag from -(N-1) to N-1, or only up to maxlag. scaleopt is 'none' (default), 'biased', 'unbiased' or 'coeff' (peak 1 at lag 0 for autocorrelation). A shorter vector is zero-padded. Only vectors are supported.

xlabel.description: Labels the x axis of the current axes (or of an axes or tiledlayout handle); accepts the same options as title and returns a Text handle on request.

xlim.description: Sets or returns the x-axis limits of the current axes. An infinite end keeps that side automatic, e.g. xlim([0 Inf]).

xor.description: Element-wise exclusive OR: true where exactly one of A and B is nonzero.

xtickangle.description: Rotates the x-axis tick labels by angle degrees, or returns the current rotation.

xticklabels.description: Sets the text of the tick labels on the x axis (yticklabels: the y axis) at the current tick positions, in order; extra labels are dropped and missing ones left blank. labels is a cell array, string array or char matrix (numbers are also accepted). With no input, returns the labels as a cell column; 'auto' restores automatic labels.

xticks.description: Puts the x-axis tick marks at the values in v ([] removes them), returns the visible tick positions, or goes back to automatic ticks.

ylabel.description: Labels the y axis of the current axes (or of an axes or tiledlayout handle); accepts the same options as title and returns a Text handle on request.

ylim.description: Sets or returns the y-axis limits of the current axes (the active side with yyaxis). An infinite end keeps that side automatic, e.g. ylim([0 Inf]).

ytickangle.description: Rotates the y-axis tick labels by angle degrees, or returns the current rotation.

yticklabels.description: Sets the text of the tick labels on the x axis (yticklabels: the y axis) at the current tick positions, in order; extra labels are dropped and missing ones left blank. labels is a cell array, string array or char matrix (numbers are also accepted). With no input, returns the labels as a cell column; 'auto' restores automatic labels.

yticks.description: Puts the y-axis tick marks at the values in v ([] removes them), returns the visible tick positions, or goes back to automatic ticks.

yyaxis.description: Gives the current axes a second y axis on the right. Later plots, labels and limits apply to the chosen side; each side has its own colour.

zeros.description: Array filled with 0. With no size it returns the scalar 0; n gives an n-by-n result; (m, n) or [m n] gives m-by-n; more sizes such as (m, n, p) give an N-D array. A class name such as 'int32' or 'single' sets the type. Example: zeros(2, 3) is a 2-by-3 matrix of zeros.

zlabel.description: Labels the z axis of the current 3-D axes; ignored on 2-D axes.

zlim.description: Sets or returns the z-axis limits of the current 3-D axes; an infinite end keeps the current limit on that side.

zscore.description: Standardizes data: subtracts the mean and divides by the standard deviation (N-1 normalization, or N with flag 1) along the first dimension whose size is not 1. Constant data gives zeros.

zticks.description: Sets or returns the z-axis tick positions of 3-D axes.
